<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><strong>Why is Channel A mono-signature while Channel B is bi-signature? A structural diagnosis.</strong> The four tables above raise a foundational question that demands an explicit structural answer. Channel A, the algebraic-symmetry reading of <em>dx₄/dt = ic</em>, is <em>uniformly Lorentzian</em> across every instance in the corpus — Table 2&#8217;s Euclidean column is empty. Channel B, the geometric-propagation reading of <em>dx₄/dt = ic</em>, is <em>bi-signature</em> — Table 3 has both columns populated with paired phenomena. <em>Why?</em> What is the deep structural reason for this asymmetry? We give the diagnosis in four steps. The diagnosis is itself a structural theorem about the McGucken Principle and, to our knowledge, has not been articulated elsewhere in the foundational-physics literature.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><em>Step 1: Locate the imaginary unit i.</em> The principle <em>dx₄/dt = ic</em> contains a single load-bearing imaginary unit <em>i</em>, multiplying the rate <em>c</em>. The <em>i</em> is not a notational decoration; it is the algebraic record of <em>x₄</em>&#8216;s perpendicularity to the three spatial dimensions <em>x₁, x₂, x₃</em> — the foundational geometric fact that the fourth direction of spacetime is <em>not parallel to any spatial direction</em> but is <em>square-rooted-negative</em> against the spatial three-slice. The <em>i</em> is what makes the four-velocity budget <em>u^μ u_μ = −c²</em> hold with a negative sign in the time component, what makes the Minkowski line element <em>ds² = dx² + dy² + dz² − c²dt²</em> have the (−,+,+,+) signature, and what makes the McGucken-Wick rotation a non-trivial rotation rather than a passive relabelling. The structural status of this <em>i</em> — whether it sits <em>interior</em> to a derivation as a fixed algebraic fact, or <em>exterior</em> to a derivation as a coordinate convention available for rotation — is the key to the signature asymmetry of the McGucken Duality.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><em>Step 2: The i is interior to Channel A.</em> Channel A reads <em>dx₄/dt = ic</em> as a statement about <em>invariance</em>: the rate <em>ic</em> is unchanged under translations, rotations, and Lorentz boosts that respect the McGucken-foliation structure. The unitary representations of these symmetries (Stone&#8217;s theorem on translation, the Wigner classification on Poincaré, the Stone–von Neumann theorem on canonical commutation) involve operators of the form <em>exp(−is p̂_i/ℏ)</em>, <em>exp(−iĤt/ℏ)</em>, <em>exp(−iθ Ĵ_z/ℏ)</em> — <em>every one of which carries the i interior</em>. The <em>i</em> in these unitary operators is <em>the same i</em> that appears in <em>dx₄/dt = ic</em>: it is the algebraic record of the perpendicularity of <em>x₄</em> that propagates from the McGucken Principle into the operator algebra of Stone-theorem unitaries. Applying the McGucken-Wick rotation to a Channel A unitary — i.e., performing the exteriorisation operation that removes the <em>i</em> from the interior of the operator — replaces the unitary group with a different mathematical object: an exponentiated semigroup <em>exp(−τ Ĥ/ℏ)</em>. The result is <em>no longer a Channel A reading</em>: a semigroup of self-adjoint exponentials is <em>not</em> a unitary representation of a symmetry group; it is a propagation-evolution kernel. The <em>i</em> is therefore not available for exteriorisation in Channel A: it is the structural feature being read as the invariance content of the principle, and removing it would dissolve Channel A entirely. Hence Channel A is Lorentzian-locked. The Lorentzian signature <em>is</em> the <em>i</em> in <em>dx₄/dt = ic</em> read as the invariance content of the principle.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><em>Step 3: The i is exteriorisable in Channel B.</em> Channel B reads <em>dx₄/dt = ic</em> as a statement about <em>propagation</em>: the rate <em>c</em> drives spherical expansion of <em>x₄</em> from every spacetime event, producing iterated McGucken Spheres on which wavefronts, paths, and entropies propagate. The <em>i</em> in <em>dx₄/dt = ic</em> enters Channel B through the <em>phase accumulation rule</em>: each iterated McGucken Sphere path <em>γ</em> carries the phase factor <em>exp(iS[γ]/ℏ)</em> by virtue of the Compton-frequency oscillation <em>ω_C = mc²/ℏ</em> of <em>x₄</em>-phase along <em>γ</em> (Proposition L.3). But here a structural option appears that is <em>not available in Channel A</em>: the geometric propagation along iterated McGucken Spheres can be <em>re-parameterised</em> by treating the <em>τ = x₄/c coordinate axis</em> as a real positive coordinate rather than as an imaginary one. Under this re-parameterisation, the phase factor <em>exp(iS[γ]/ℏ)</em> (Lorentzian reading, <em>i</em> interior) becomes the measure factor <em>exp(−S_E[γ]/ℏ)</em> (Euclidean reading, <em>i</em> exteriorised onto the <em>τ</em>-axis as a real positive coordinate; cf. Theorem 7.9, Step 3). The <em>same iterated McGucken Sphere expansion</em> generates both readings, with the <em>i</em> operating <em>interior</em> in the Lorentzian reading and <em>exterior</em> (on the <em>τ</em>-coordinate axis) in the Euclidean reading. The McGucken-Wick rotation <em>t → −iτ, τ = x₄/c</em> — the <em>physically-forced</em> rotation that exists because <em>dx₄/dt = ic</em> is a real physical statement about an actually expanding fourth dimension, not a formal analytic-continuation device on a complex <em>t</em>-plane — is, on this diagnosis, the <em>exteriorisation operation</em> on the <em>i</em>: it moves the <em>i</em> from the <em>interior of the path weight</em> (phase factor <em>exp(iS/ℏ)</em>) to the <em>exterior of the coordinate frame</em> (real <em>τ</em>-axis on the real McGucken manifold). The McGucken-Wick rotation is therefore the structural operation by which Channel B&#8217;s bi-signature character is realised, and <em>it is available only in Channel B because Channel B treats the i as a propagation phase that can be re-located, not as the invariance content that defines the algebraic reading</em>. The exteriorisation is <em>physically forced</em> by the existence of <em>dx₄/dt = ic</em> as the real dynamical motion of the fourth dimension; Wick&#8217;s 1954 formal device, by contrast, has no physical mechanism for the exteriorisation and is therefore strictly weaker than the McGucken-Wick rotation.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><em>Step 4: The historical-priority asymmetry as symptom.</em> The structural diagnosis of Steps 2–3 has a historical surface that is worth recording. The <em>algebraic-symmetry reading</em> of <em>x₄</em> has been substantially developed since Minkowski 1908 [5]: <em>x₄ = ict</em> is a notational identity at the level of metric signature, the unitary representations of Stone, Wigner, von Neumann, Heisenberg, Dirac, and Stone–von Neumann are the standard apparatus of quantum mechanics and quantum field theory by 1930, and the Lorentzian operator algebra of Channel A is by now a century-old mature subject. The <em>geometric-propagation reading</em> of <em>x₄</em>, by contrast, was not developed at the foundational level until the McGucken corpus introduced <em>dx₄/dt = ic</em> as a dynamical principle [3, W, F, MQF, MGT, GRQM]: prior to the McGucken framework, the imaginary direction was treated <em>algebraically</em> (Minkowski 1908) or as a <em>formal calculational device</em> (Wick 1954, Symanzik 1969, Osterwalder–Schrader 1973), with no recognition that the <em>i</em> in the metric is the algebraic record of an <em>actual physical motion</em> of the fourth dimension at velocity <em>c</em>. The geometric reading is therefore <em>new</em>, and it is the operation that <em>exposes the i for exteriorisation</em>: once <em>x₄</em> is recognised as a real fourth direction whose expansion at rate <em>c</em> is the foundational physical postulate, the <em>τ = x₄/c</em> re-parameterisation becomes a <em>real coordinate identification on a real manifold</em> rather than a <em>formal contour deformation on a complex t-plane</em>, and the Euclidean reading of Channel B becomes available as a <em>physical</em> reading rather than as a <em>calculational shadow</em>.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">This is why the Euclidean column of Channel A took 75 years to never quite materialise — Symanzik, Osterwalder–Schrader, Glimm–Jaffe, Streater–Wightman, Wightman, Haag, Doplicher–Haag–Roberts, and others made enormous progress on Euclidean <em>Channel B</em> (the constructive Euclidean field theory programme, OS reflection positivity, KMS condition, lattice gauge theory, stochastic quantization) but did not produce a <em>Euclidean Channel A</em> because the structural obstruction was not historical accident but the position of the <em>i</em> in the McGucken Principle: the <em>i</em> is <em>interior to Channel A&#8217;s reading of dx₄/dt = ic</em>, and exteriorising it dissolves Channel A into Channel B in the rotated signature. The historical priority of the algebraic reading (Minkowski 1908) over the geometric reading (McGucken 2026) is therefore a <em>symptom</em> of the structural fact, not its cause: the algebraic reading kept the <em>i</em> permanently interior because Channel A is <em>the reading that requires the i interior</em>, and the geometric reading is the operation by which the <em>i</em> becomes available for exteriorisation. The McGucken Principle is what makes both readings simultaneously available; the four-table structure of §2.5 records the consequence.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">The deep reason, in one sentence: <strong>Channel A is Lorentzian-locked because the i in dx₄/dt = ic is interior to the algebraic-symmetry reading, where it is the invariance content itself; Channel B is bi-signature because the i in dx₄/dt = ic is exteriorisable from the geometric-propagation reading, where it is the phase coefficient that can be rotated by the McGucken-Wick rotation onto the real τ-coordinate axis without changing the underlying iterated McGucken Sphere expansion.</strong></p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><em>Step 5: Status of this structural diagnosis in the foundational-physics literature.</em> The structural fact diagnosed in Steps 1–4 — that Channel A is Lorentzian-locked because the <em>i</em> is interior to it, that Channel B is bi-signature because the <em>i</em> is exteriorisable from it, and that the McGucken-Wick rotation is the <em>exteriorisation operation</em> on the <em>i</em> that converts Lorentzian Channel B into Euclidean Channel B (and that converts Channel A into Channel B in the rotated signature) — is, to the best of our reading of the prior literature, <em>a structural theorem about the McGucken Duality that has not been articulated elsewhere in foundational physics</em>. The constructive Euclidean field theory programme (Symanzik 1969 [70]; Osterwalder–Schrader 1973 [«1973»]; Glimm–Jaffe [«1981»]; Streater–Wightman) recognised that the Euclidean signature reading of QFT is a <em>Channel B</em> object (path integrals, partition functions, correlation functions, OS reflection positivity, KMS condition, Matsubara formalism, lattice gauge theory) and developed the Euclidean side of the duality to substantial depth, but no published account in this tradition has articulated <em>why there is no parallel Euclidean Channel A</em> — why the constructive programme produces Euclidean path integrals but no Euclidean Stone-theorem analogues, no Euclidean Noether currents on real Euclidean manifolds, no Euclidean unitary symmetry algebras. The structural obstruction is the position of the <em>i</em> in <em>dx₄/dt = ic</em>: the <em>i</em> is interior to the algebraic-symmetry content of the principle and exterior(isable) only from the geometric-propagation content, and the exteriorisation operation is the McGucken-Wick rotation read as a <em>real coordinate identification on a real four-manifold</em>. Both ingredients — the position-of-<em>i</em> diagnosis and the physical-mechanism reading of the McGucken-Wick rotation — are McGucken-framework constructions. Identifying the symmetry-content / propagation-content asymmetry and the structural status of the imaginary unit in the McGucken Principle as the source of the asymmetry is one of the structural contributions of the present paper.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">The remainder of the paper develops the McGucken Duality in detail: §3 develops Channel A for GR (factorization of Diff(M)-invariance, Lovelock + Newtonian closure); §4 develops Channel B for GR and thermodynamics (geometric Second Law, area law, Unruh temperature, Clausius chain, Compton-coupling Brownian mechanism); §6 establishes the Signature-Bridging Theorem stating that Channel A and Channel B agree on <em>G_μν</em>; §7 develops both channels for QM (Hamiltonian route Hamiltonian, Lagrangian route Lagrangian, both producing <em>[q̂, p̂] = iℏ</em>) and concludes with the Universal McGucken Channel B Theorem identifying the Channel B contents of QM, statistical mechanics, and GR as Wick-rotations of a single underlying geometric object — iterated McGucken Sphere expansion.</p>



<h3 class="wp-block-heading">§2.6 The Physical Reading of <em>dx₄/dt = ic</em> and Why It Matters</h3>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">The McGucken Principle <em>dx₄/dt = ic</em> is <em>physically and not merely formally</em> distinct from Minkowski&#8217;s 1908 notation <em>x</em>₄ = <em>ict</em>. The two equations are mathematically related by one calculus operation in either direction — Minkowski&#8217;s static <em>x</em>₄ = <em>ict</em> is the integral of <em>dx₄/dt = ic</em>, and <em>dx₄/dt = ic</em> is the derivative of <em>x</em>₄ = <em>ict</em> — but their <em>physical content</em> is asymmetric, and the entire content of the present paper rests on the asymmetry. This subsection emphasizes what the physical reading is, why it differs from the static reading, and what is lost if the principle is treated as a mere mathematical identity. The emphasis is required because the McGucken framework&#8217;s derivational content vanishes entirely if <em>dx₄/dt = ic</em> is read only as the calculus derivative of <em>x</em>₄ = <em>ict</em>. The treatment follows [GRQM, §2] where this distinction is developed at full length in seven sectors of physics.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><strong>The static reading.</strong> Minkowski&#8217;s 1908 paper <em>Raum und Zeit</em> [5] introduced <em>x</em>₄ = <em>ict</em> as a coordinate label that renders the spacetime metric pseudo-Euclidean: under <em>x</em>₄ = <em>ict</em>, the Minkowski line element <em>ds² = dx₁² + dx₂² + dx₃² − c² dt²</em> becomes <em>ds² = dx₁² + dx₂² + dx₃² + dx₄²</em>, i.e., the Euclidean four-distance. The substitution is <em>notational</em>: the imaginary unit <em>i</em> is a bookkeeping device that converts Lorentzian signature to Euclidean form, and <em>x</em>₄ is a coordinate label whose only role is to scale <em>t</em> by <em>ic</em> for this purpose. The textbook tradition for over a century has read <em>x</em>₄ in this static, notational sense: <em>x</em>₄ is a coordinate, <em>i</em> is bookkeeping, and the equation <em>x</em>₄ = <em>ict</em> delivers exactly the spacetime metric and nothing more. Special relativity follows from the metric; general relativity is layered on top through the separately postulated Equivalence Principle, geodesic hypothesis, and field equations; quantum mechanics is developed independently of relativistic geometry through Schrödinger&#8217;s 1926 wave equation and Heisenberg&#8217;s 1925 matrix mechanics, with no derivational connection to <em>x</em>₄ = <em>ict</em>. The static reading delivers the Minkowski metric and the kinematic content of special relativity, and nothing else.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><strong>The physical reading.</strong> The McGucken reading is the inverse. <em>dx₄/dt = ic</em> is read here not as a formal convenience of notation but as a <em>dynamical, physical, geometric statement</em>: the fourth dimension is in <em>active, isotropic, monotone, invariant expansion at rate c</em>. (i) <em>Active</em>: not a passive coordinate label but a physical process. (ii) <em>Isotropic</em>: spherically symmetric from every event (the source of Huygens&#8217; Principle, holography, and the McGucken Sphere as universal geometric atom). (iii) <em>Monotone</em>: +<em>ic</em> only, not −<em>ic</em> (the source of the arrow of time, the strict Second Law, and the +<em>ic</em>-orientation that breaks time-reversal at the macroscopic level). (iv) <em>Invariant</em>: the rate is <em>c</em> in every frame, at every event, regardless of the presence of matter (the source of Lorentz invariance, special relativity, and the invariant/deformable split of §2.4 that produces gravity).</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">The physical content is asymmetric to the mathematical content: <em>dx₄/dt = ic</em> is the dynamical statement of an actual physical motion of the fourth dimension; <em>x</em>₄ = <em>ict</em> is the integrated kinematic shadow of that motion at coordinate time <em>t</em>. The first describes what is <em>physically happening</em>; the second describes the coordinate position that follows from what is physically happening. The textbook tradition for over a century has worked with the integrated shadow without recognizing the dynamical reality it shadows. The discovery is not the recognition that <em>x</em>₄ = <em>ict</em> can be differentiated to give <em>dx₄/dt = ic</em>; this is a one-line calculus operation. The discovery is the recognition that the <em>physical reality</em> underlying the formal relation <em>x</em>₄ = <em>ict</em> is an actual physical motion of the fourth dimension at rate <em>c</em> in a spherically symmetric manner from every spacetime event, and that this physical statement — <em>dx₄/dt = ic</em> — is the foundational principle from which the entire content of foundational physics descends.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><strong>What is lost without the physical reading.</strong> The dual-channel structure (§2.5) requires the physical reading. Channel A is the invariance content of an actual physical motion; without a physical motion, there is no invariance group of any depth — only the algebraic content of <em>x</em>₄ = <em>ict</em> as a coordinate identity. Channel B is the wavefront content of an actual physical spherical expansion; without a physical expansion, there is no wavefront — only an algebraic identity with no spherical geometry. Specifically, without the physical reading:</p>



<ul class="wp-block-list">
<li>(1) The McGucken Duality (Channel A as algebraic-symmetry, Channel B as geometric-propagation, descending as parallel sibling consequences from the same principle) loses its content because there is no principle to descend from — there is only an algebraic identity <em>x</em>₄ = <em>ict</em> with no physical referent.</li>



<li>(2) The Hilbert variational derivation of <em>G_μν</em> (Channel A at the gravitational tier) and the Jacobson thermodynamic derivation of <em>G_μν</em> (Channel B at the gravitational tier) revert to two disjoint mathematical objects with no shared origin, and the Signature-Bridging Theorem of §6 reduces to the observation that two independent derivations happen to agree.</li>



<li>(3) The Hamiltonian route to <em>[q̂, p̂] = iℏ</em> (Channel A at the matter tier) and the Lagrangian route to <em>[q̂, p̂] = iℏ</em> (Channel B at the matter tier) revert to two disjoint derivations with no shared physical origin; the structural overdetermination of Theorem 7.1 becomes a remarkable coincidence rather than a forced identity.</li>



<li>(4) The Universal McGucken Channel B Theorem (§7.9) fails entirely. The Feynman path integral (Lorentzian) and the Wiener process (Euclidean) are not Wick-rotations of each other via <em>τ = x₄/c</em> on a real four-manifold; they are formally-related mathematical objects via Kac–Nelson without physical mechanism. The structural unification of quantum mechanics and classical statistical mechanics dissolves.</li>



<li>(5) The Huygens-equals-Holography identification (Theorem 7.9.5) fails because there is no McGucken Sphere as a physical wavefront; the holographic principle reverts to its previous unexplained status, and the bulk-boundary encoding mechanism is again a mystery.</li>



<li>(6) The geometric Second Law (Theorem 4.1) and the strict particle-level rate <em>dS/dt = (3/2)k_B/t</em> (Proposition 4.5.4) revert to statistical postulates rather than geometric consequences. The Loschmidt dissolution (Theorem 4.6.1) and the Past Hypothesis dissolution (Theorem 4.6.2) fail because there is no +<em>ic</em> branch selection to provide the structural asymmetry.</li>



<li>(7) The Wick rotation <em>t → −iτ</em> reverts to a formal calculational device justified by analyticity of correlation functions, with no physical reading. The 75 years of constructive QFT, lattice gauge theory, stochastic quantization, and thermal field theory that have used the Wick rotation as a working tool become, on the static reading, 75 years of inexplicable empirical success without foundational mechanism.</li>



<li>(8) The reduction of the dimensional content of physics from ≳ 10³ bits of independent inputs to ≲ 10² bits of a single foundational principle (§10.7) fails because there is no foundational principle of physical content — only an algebraic identity that delivers the Minkowski metric and nothing else.</li>
</ul>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">The total cost of treating <em>dx₄/dt = ic</em> as a mere mathematical equation rather than as a physical principle is the loss of every theorem in this paper, the loss of the closure of the QM–GR foundational gap, and the reversion of physics to the unresolved century-long state in which this paper found it.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><strong>The mathematical reading delivers nothing beyond the Minkowski metric. The physical reading delivers all of foundational physics.</strong> This asymmetry is not metaphorical. It is the structural content of the present paper, and the content of every chain of theorems in the McGucken corpus [W, F, MQF, MGT]. The mathematical relation between <em>dx₄/dt = ic</em> and <em>x</em>₄ = <em>ict</em> is one calculus operation; the <em>physical recognition</em> that <em>dx₄/dt = ic</em> describes an actual physical motion of the fourth dimension has been one century in coming. The integrated form <em>x</em>₄ = <em>ict</em> has been on the page since 1908. What was missing for over a century — and what the McGucken framework supplies — is the recognition that this integrated form is the kinematic shadow of an actual physical motion: <em>dx₄/dt = ic</em>, with the fourth dimension expanding at <em>c</em> in a spherically symmetric manner from every spacetime event.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">To paraphrase Armstrong&#8217;s &#8220;one small step for man, one giant leap for mankind&#8221;: <em>obtaining x₄ = ict by integration of dx₄/dt = ic, or recovering dx₄/dt = ic by differentiation of x₄ = ict, is one small step for math; recognizing that the fourth dimension is physically expanding at the velocity of light, with all the consequences this has across QM, GR, thermodynamics, and cosmology, is one giant leap for physics.</em></p>

<h2 class="wp-block-heading">§3 McGucken Channel A: Factorisation of Diff(M) Invariance</h2>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">This section derives the Einstein field equations from the McGucken Principle by the algebraic-variational route. The principal claim is that Hilbert&#8217;s diffeomorphism invariance is factored by the McGucken Principle into two physically distinct postulates: a kinematic symmetry (Diff_McG-invariance, §3.1) and a constitutive identity (the four-velocity budget, §3.2). Off shell, only Diff_McG acts; on shell, full Diff(M) is recovered (§3.3). The field equations follow by Lovelock + Newtonian limit (§3.4).</p>



<h3 class="wp-block-heading">§3.1 The foliation-preserving subgroup Diff_McG(M)</h3>



<blockquote class="wp-block-quote is-layout-flow wp-block-quote-is-layout-flow">
<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><strong>Definition 3.1.</strong> <em>Let M be a smooth four-manifold equipped with a global function x</em>₀: <em>M → ℝ whose level surfaces Σ_t are the x₄-foliation slices. The</em> foliation-preserving diffeomorphism group <em>Diff_McG(M) is the subgroup of Diff(M) generated by vector fields</em></p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><em>ξ^μ = (ξ⁰(x⁰), ξ^i(x⁰, x^j))</em> <em>(3.1)</em></p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><em>where ξ⁰ depends only on x⁰ and ξ^i may depend on all coordinates.</em></p>
</blockquote>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">The physical content is direct. The McGucken Principle (2.1) fixes the rate of <em>x</em>₄-advance to <em>ic</em> at every point. Reparametrisations of the <em>x</em>₀-coordinate are constrained to be rigid (depending only on <em>x</em>₀ itself) because <em>x</em>₄-advance per coordinate time is the <em>invariant</em> of the foliation; rescaling <em>x</em>₀ non-rigidly would change this rate at different points and violate (2.1). Spatial diffeomorphisms are unconstrained because space is <em>deformable</em>.</p>



<blockquote class="wp-block-quote is-layout-flow wp-block-quote-is-layout-flow">
<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><strong>Lemma 3.2.</strong> <em>Diff_McG(M) is a strict subgroup of Diff(M). In particular, the full four-dimensional diffeomorphisms generated by ξ⁰(x⁰, x^j) with non-trivial spatial dependence are not in Diff_McG.</em></p>
</blockquote>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><em>Proof.</em> The general vector field on <em>M</em> is <em>ξ^μ = (ξ⁰(x⁰, x^i), ξ^i(x⁰, x^j))</em>. Restricting <em>ξ⁰</em> to depend only on <em>x⁰</em> yields a proper subgroup, since vector fields with <em>∂ξ⁰/∂x^i ≠ 0</em> are not of the form (3.1). ∎</p>



<h3 class="wp-block-heading">§3.2 The constitutive identity</h3>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">The second postulate of Channel A is the constitutive content of the McGucken Principle: every massive particle obeys <em>u^μ u_μ = −c²</em> as a <em>pointwise dynamical identity</em>, not as a coordinate definition. This is the four-velocity budget of §2.2.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">The stress tensor for a fluid of such particles is constructed in the standard way:</p>



<blockquote class="wp-block-quote is-layout-flow wp-block-quote-is-layout-flow">
<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><em>T^μν = (ρc² + p) u^μ u^ν/c² + p g^μν</em> <em>(3.2)</em></p>
</blockquote>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">with the McGucken constraint <em>u^μ u_μ = −c²</em> enforced pointwise. For a free particle, <em>T^μν = (ρc²) u^μ u^ν/c²</em> with the same constraint.</p>



<h3 class="wp-block-heading">§3.3 Noether&#8217;s second theorem applied to Diff_McG, and on-shell enhancement</h3>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Apply Noether&#8217;s second theorem [10] to the matter action <em>S_M[φ, g_μν]</em> invariant under Diff_McG(M). Before doing so, we note a structural strengthening of the present derivation supplied by McGucken (2026) [F]: <em>Noether&#8217;s theorem is itself a theorem of the McGucken Symmetry dx₄/dt = ic</em>, not an independent mathematical input. The derivation chain established in [F, Theorem 18.4] runs:</p>



<blockquote class="wp-block-quote is-layout-flow wp-block-quote-is-layout-flow">
<p class="wp-block-paragraph">dx₄/dt = ic → Lorentzian interval (via i² = −1 in the metric) → Poincaré group ISO(1,3) as the invariance group of the interval → Kleinian structure (ISO(1,3), SO<math><semantics><mrow><msup><mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">+</mo></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">^{+}</annotation></semantics></math>+(1,3)) → Noether&#8217;s first theorem on continuous symmetries → conserved currents *∂_μ j^μ = 0*.</p>
</blockquote>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Noether&#8217;s second theorem (the gauge-symmetry refinement used in the present section) follows by the same structural template applied to local rather than global symmetries: Noether&#8217;s two theorems are the two faces of one structural fact about the variational principle on the McGucken-Kleinian manifold. Consequently, the Channel A derivation here rests on no mathematical input external to dx₄/dt = ic — Noether is an intermediate theorem on the path from the McGucken Principle to G_μν, not a separately postulated machinery. This is consistent with the broader programme of [F], which establishes Lorentz, Poincaré, Noether, gauge, quantum-unitary, CPT, supersymmetry, diffeomorphism, and the standard string-theoretic dualities and symmetries all as theorems of the McGucken Symmetry.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">With this strengthening noted, the application of Noether&#8217;s second theorem to the Diff_McG-invariant matter action proceeds as follows. The conservation laws that drop out are:</p>



<blockquote class="wp-block-quote is-layout-flow wp-block-quote-is-layout-flow">
<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><em>∇_i T^iν = 0</em> (spatial conservation on each <em>x</em>₄-slice) <em>(3.3)</em></p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><em>∂_t</em> ∫_Σ <em>T^0ν √h d³x = 0</em> (integrated time conservation) <em>(3.4)</em></p>
</blockquote>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">where Σ is a spatial slice and <em>h_ij</em> is the induced spatial metric. These are <em>weaker</em> than the full local conservation <em>∇_μ T^μν = 0</em> that Hilbert&#8217;s diffeomorphism invariance gives, because Diff_McG is a strict subgroup of Diff(M) (Lemma 3.2).</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">The key structural step of Channel A is that the gap between (3.3)–(3.4) and the full local conservation is closed by the <em>constitutive identity</em> (3.2) combined with the equations of motion.</p>



<blockquote class="wp-block-quote is-layout-flow wp-block-quote-is-layout-flow">
<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><strong>Theorem 3.3 (on-shell enhancement).</strong> <em>Given:</em> <em>(i) Diff_McG(M)-invariance of the matter action;</em> <em>(ii) the constitutive identity u^μu_μ = −c² (pointwise);</em> <em>(iii) the matter equations of motion;</em> <em>the local conservation ∇_μ T^μν = 0 holds. Consequently, the full diffeomorphism Diff(M) acts as a symmetry on shell.</em></p>
</blockquote>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><em>Proof.</em> Differentiating the stress tensor T^μν = (ρc² + p)u^μu^ν/c² + pg^μν gives</p>



<blockquote class="wp-block-quote is-layout-flow wp-block-quote-is-layout-flow">
<p class="wp-block-paragraph">∇_μ T^μν = ∇_μ[(ρc² + p)u^μ/c²] u^ν + (ρc² + p)u^μ ∇_μ u^ν/c² + g^μν ∂_μ p. (\dag)</p>
</blockquote>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Contracting (\dag) with u_ν and using u^ν u_ν = −c² (constitutive identity, postulate (ii)) together with u_ν ∇_μ u^ν = 0 (which follows from differentiating u^ν u_ν = −c² and is the dynamical content of the constraint), the first term gives −c² ∇_μ[(ρc² + p)u^μ/c²], the second vanishes, and the third gives u^μ ∂_μ p. The continuity equation ∇_μ(ρ u^μ) = 0 (matter equation of motion, postulate (iii)) plus standard thermodynamic identities close (\dag) to yield u_ν ∇_μ T^μν = 0.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Projecting (\dag) orthogonal to u^ν using the spatial projector h^ν_λ = δ^ν_λ + u^ν u_λ/c² and using the Euler equation (ρc² + p)u^μ ∇_μ u_λ = −h^μ_λ ∂_μ p (postulate (iii), the matter equation of motion in its Euler form) yields h^ν_λ ∇_μ T^μλ = 0.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Together, u_ν ∇_μ T^μν = 0 and h^ν_λ ∇_μ T^μλ = 0 span all four directions in the tangent space, so ∇_μ T^μν = 0. The off-shell Diff_McG-invariance (postulate (i)) provided the spatial conservation (3.3) and the integrated time conservation (3.4); postulates (ii) and (iii) supply the additional information needed to upgrade these to local conservation in all four components.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Once ∇_μ T^μν = 0 holds, the Bianchi-compatible field equations G_μν ∝ T_μν are consistent with arbitrary diffeomorphisms acting on both sides; the action is invariant under full Diff(M) on shell. ∎</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">The structural meaning: the McGucken Principle is <em>stronger</em> than diffeomorphism invariance because it determines <em>which</em> diffeomorphisms are off-shell symmetries (only Diff_McG) and <em>why</em> the full Diff(M) is recovered on-shell (because the four-velocity budget is consistent with arbitrary reparametrisation of the worldline). Hilbert&#8217;s setup, by contrast, postulates full Diff(M)-invariance from the outset and treats this as primitive.</p>



<h3 class="wp-block-heading">§3.4 The field equations from Lovelock and the Newtonian limit</h3>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">With <em>∇_μ T^μν = 0</em> established (Theorem 3.3), the geometric side of the field equations is forced by Lovelock&#8217;s theorem [12]:</p>



<blockquote class="wp-block-quote is-layout-flow wp-block-quote-is-layout-flow">
<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><strong>Lovelock&#8217;s theorem (1971).</strong> <em>In four dimensions, the unique divergence-free symmetric rank-2 tensor built from the metric g_μν and its first two derivatives, linear in second derivatives, is</em></p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><em>L_μν = αG_μν + βg_μν</em></p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><em>for constants α, β, where G_μν = R_μν − (1/2)Rg_μν is the Einstein tensor.</em></p>
</blockquote>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Setting <em>L_μν = κT_μν</em> with <em>κ = 8πG/c⁴</em> and <em>β = Λ</em> gives</p>



<blockquote class="wp-block-quote is-layout-flow wp-block-quote-is-layout-flow">
<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><em>G_μν + Λg_μν = (8πG/c⁴) T_μν.</em> <em>(3.5)</em></p>
</blockquote>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">The coupling constant <em>κ = 8πG/c⁴</em> is fixed by demanding agreement with the Newtonian limit. In the weak-field static limit <em>g_00 = −(1 + 2Φ/c²)</em>, <em>g_ij = δ_ij</em>, with <em>T^00 = ρc²</em> dominant, equation (3.5) reduces to Poisson&#8217;s equation <em>∇²Φ = 4πGρ</em> [11, §17.4]. The factor <em>8π/c⁴</em> is forced by this matching.</p>



<blockquote class="wp-block-quote is-layout-flow wp-block-quote-is-layout-flow">
<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><strong>Theorem 3.4 (Channel A output).</strong> <em>The Einstein field equations G_μν + Λg_μν = (8πG/c⁴) T_μν follow from:</em> <em>(i) Diff_McG(M)-invariance of the matter action (from x₄-foliation invariance, a corollary of dx₄/dt = ic);</em> <em>(ii) the four-velocity budget u^μu_μ = −c² (the constitutive content of dx₄/dt = ic);</em> <em>(iii) Lovelock&#8217;s theorem (4D uniqueness of divergence-free Einstein tensor);</em> <em>(iv) the Newtonian limit (coupling constant matching).</em></p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><em>Postulates (i) and (ii) are both theorems of dx₄/dt = ic. Noether&#8217;s second theorem, which translates (i) into the conservation law applied via Theorem 3.3, is itself a theorem of dx₄/dt = ic via the chain established in [F, Theorem 18.4]. Postulates (iii) and (iv) are standard.</em></p>
</blockquote>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">This is the Channel A derivation. It does not replace Hilbert; it <em>factors</em> Hilbert&#8217;s diffeomorphism invariance into two physically distinct components, both grounded in <em>dx₄/dt = ic</em>.</p>



<hr class="wp-block-separator has-alpha-channel-opacity" />



<h2 class="wp-block-heading">§4 McGucken Channel B: Thermodynamic Derivation, Self-Contained</h2>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">This section derives the Einstein field equations from the McGucken Principle by the thermodynamic route, <em>self-containedly</em>. Every input that Jacobson&#8217;s 1995 derivation [2] treats as a postulate — area-law entropy, monotone entropy increase, the Unruh temperature, the holographic screen — is here derived from <em>dx₄/dt = ic</em>. The Clausius relation <em>δQ = TdS</em> applied to local Rindler horizons then yields the field equations by Jacobson&#8217;s chain.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">The previous McGucken paper on Jacobson&#8217;s framework [13] established the conceptual identification of these inputs. The present section gives the <em>standalone</em> derivation chain: each input is constructed mathematically from (2.1) without external thermodynamic or quantum-statistical postulates beyond the Clausius relation itself.</p>



<h3 class="wp-block-heading">§4.1 Geometric Second Law: dS/dt &gt; 0 from isotropic x₄-expansion</h3>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Consider an ensemble of <em>N</em> particles at positions {<em>r⃗_α</em>}, <em>α</em> = 1, …, <em>N</em>, at coordinate time <em>t</em>. By the McGucken Principle, each particle is advanced by <em>x</em>₄&#8217;s isotropic expansion at every infinitesimal time step <em>δt</em>: the particle moves a distance <em>cδt</em> in a direction <em>n̂</em> drawn uniformly from the unit sphere <em>S²</em>. This is the kinematic content of <em>dx₄/dt = ic</em> projected onto the spatial slice — the McGucken Sphere of expansion intersecting <em>x</em>₁<em>x</em>₂<em>x</em>₃ as a 2-sphere of radius <em>cδt</em> about every event [13, §III.1].</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">The probability distribution <em>P(r⃗, t)</em> of the particle position satisfies the isotropic diffusion equation</p>



<blockquote class="wp-block-quote is-layout-flow wp-block-quote-is-layout-flow">
<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><em>∂P/∂t = D ∇² P, D = c²δt_p/6</em> <em>(4.1)</em></p>
</blockquote>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">where <em>δt_p = √(ℏG/c⁵)</em> is the Planck time, the fundamental time step at which <em>x</em>₄ advances by one Planck length <em>ℓ_p = √(ℏG/c³)</em> [3, 4, 13]. The diffusion coefficient <em>D = c²δt_p/6</em> follows from the standard random-walk relation <em>⟨r²⟩ = 6Dt</em> for isotropic three-dimensional motion with step size <em>cδt_p</em> per step.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">The Boltzmann–Gibbs differential entropy of <em>P</em> with Gaussian initial condition is</p>



<blockquote class="wp-block-quote is-layout-flow wp-block-quote-is-layout-flow">
<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><em>S(t) = −k_B</em> ∫ <em>P ln P d³r = (3/2) k_B ln(4πeDt) + const</em> <em>(4.2)</em></p>
</blockquote>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">and therefore</p>



<blockquote class="wp-block-quote is-layout-flow wp-block-quote-is-layout-flow">
<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><em>dS/dt = (3/2) k_B / t &gt; 0 for all t &gt; 0.</em> <em>(4.3)</em></p>
</blockquote>



<blockquote class="wp-block-quote is-layout-flow wp-block-quote-is-layout-flow">
<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><strong>Theorem 4.1 (Geometric Second Law).</strong> <em>Given the physical principle <strong>dx₄/dt = ic</strong> — the dynamical statement that the fourth dimension expands at velocity c in a spherically symmetric manner at every spacetime event — the Boltzmann–Gibbs entropy of any ensemble of particles is monotonically increasing in coordinate time:</em></p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><em>dS/dt &gt; 0.</em></p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><em><strong>Proof.</strong></em> <em>We proceed in four steps from the physical principle dx₄/dt = ic to the strict monotonicity dS/dt &gt; 0; the integrated form x₄ = ict is a kinematic shadow of the dynamical principle and plays no independent role in the derivation.</em></p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><em>Step 1 (kinematic content of dx₄/dt = ic projected onto the spatial slice). By the McGucken Principle, x₄ advances at rate ic from every spacetime event in a spherically symmetric manner. Projecting this 4-dimensional spherical expansion onto the spatial three-slice at each event produces a 2-sphere of radius cδt about that event for any infinitesimal time interval δt (the McGucken Sphere; see §2.5 and Proposition L.1). Each particle in the ensemble is therefore displaced by cδt in a direction n̂ drawn from the uniform measure on S² at every Planck-time step δt_p = √(ℏG/c⁵).</em></p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><em>Step 2 (diffusion equation from isotropic step). The probability density P(r⃗, t) of a particle position evolves under iterated isotropic Compton displacements with rms step size cδt_p per step. By the standard derivation of Brownian motion from isotropic random walks [Einstein 1905; Chandrasekhar 1943] applied with step size cδt_p and step time δt_p, the diffusion coefficient is D = (c·δt_p)²/(6 δt_p) = c²δt_p/6 and the probability density satisfies (4.1): ∂P/∂t = D ∇² P.</em></p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><em>Step 3 (Boltzmann–Gibbs entropy of the Gaussian solution). The fundamental solution of (4.1) with delta-function initial data P(r⃗, 0) = δ³(r⃗) is the Gaussian P(r⃗, t) = (4π D t)^{−3/2} exp(−r²/(4Dt)). The Boltzmann–Gibbs differential entropy is S(t) = −k_B ∫ P ln P d³r. Direct evaluation of the Gaussian entropy integral (a standard computation) gives (4.2): S(t) = (3/2) k_B ln(4π e D t) + const.</em></p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><em>Step 4 (strict monotonicity). Differentiating S(t) with respect to t gives (4.3): dS/dt = (3/2) k_B / t. Since t &gt; 0 and k_B &gt; 0, dS/dt &gt; 0 strictly for all t &gt; 0.</em></p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><em>The monotonicity is exact rather than statistical because dx₄/dt = ic specifies the +ic orientation: x₄ advances and does not retreat, so the diffusion equation (4.1) propagates probability density forward in t with no time-reversed branch in the physical dynamics. The textbook statistical Second Law (a tendency with Poincaré recurrence) reduces to the McGucken geometric Second Law (a strict monotonicity without recurrence) when the +ic-oriented physical motion underlying dx₄/dt = ic is recognised. ∎</em></p>
</blockquote>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">This is the geometric Second Law. It is <em>not</em> the statistical Second Law of Boltzmann (which is a tendency, with non-zero probability of fluctuations); it is a theorem about the <em>certain</em> monotonic advance of <em>x</em>₄ and the entropy it generates. There is no Poincaré recurrence because <em>x</em>₄ does not recur.</p>



<h3 class="wp-block-heading">§4.2 Area law: S = A/(4ℓ_p²) from x₄ quantum modes on the McGucken Sphere</h3>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">The McGucken Sphere associated with a spacetime event <em>O</em> is the 2-sphere swept out by <em>x</em>₄&#8217;s spherically symmetric expansion at radius <em>R = ct</em> from <em>O</em> [3, 4, 13]. Its area is <em>A = 4πR²</em>.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Quantise <em>x</em>₄&#8217;s expansion at the Planck scale: the fundamental wavelength of <em>x</em>₄-advance is <em>ℓ_p</em>, the Planck length [3, 4]. The number of independent quantum modes of <em>x</em>₄-advance crossing the McGucken Sphere is one mode per Planck area cell. By the standard mode-counting argument [14, §5], the number of accessible information bits stored on the sphere is</p>



<blockquote class="wp-block-quote is-layout-flow wp-block-quote-is-layout-flow">
<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><em>N_bits = A / ℓ_p²</em> <em>(4.4)</em></p>
</blockquote>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">up to a numerical factor of order unity. Identifying entropy with <em>k_B</em> times the number of bits, and fixing the numerical factor by demanding consistency with the Bekenstein–Hawking expression in the limiting case of a black hole horizon [15, 16], yields</p>



<blockquote class="wp-block-quote is-layout-flow wp-block-quote-is-layout-flow">
<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><em>S = k_B A / (4 ℓ_p²) = k_B A c³ / (4 ℏ G).</em> <em>(4.5)</em></p>
</blockquote>



<blockquote class="wp-block-quote is-layout-flow wp-block-quote-is-layout-flow">
<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><strong>Theorem 4.2 (Area law).</strong> <em>Given the McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic and the identification of the Planck length as the fundamental x₄-advance wavelength, the entropy associated with a McGucken Sphere of area A is</em></p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><em>S = k_B A / (4 ℓ_p²).</em></p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><em><strong>Proof.</strong></em> <em>Equations (4.4)–(4.5). The mode-count N_bits = A/ℓ_p² follows from one independent x₄-advance mode per Planck cell on the sphere. The numerical factor of 1/4 is fixed by matching to Bekenstein–Hawking [15, 16] and is not derived independently here. ∎</em></p>
</blockquote>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">The area law is therefore a corollary of (2.1) plus the Planck-scale quantisation of <em>x</em>₄-advance. It is not imported from black hole thermodynamics; rather, the Bekenstein–Hawking entropy is itself reinterpreted in this framework as the entropy of <em>x</em>₄-modes on a horizon-area McGucken Sphere.</p>



<h3 class="wp-block-heading">§4.3 Unruh temperature from Wick-rotated x₄-boost</h3>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">The Unruh temperature <em>T = ℏa/(2πck_B)</em> [17] is standardly derived from quantum field theory in Rindler coordinates by demanding KMS-periodicity of the vacuum two-point function under Euclidean time translation [18, 19]. The derivation imports the KMS condition and the analytic structure of the Wightman function. In the McGucken framework, the Unruh temperature is derived geometrically from the Wick-rotated <em>x</em>₄-boost.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Consider a uniformly accelerated observer with proper acceleration <em>a</em>. The observer&#8217;s worldline in Minkowski coordinates is <em>X(τ_p) = (c²/a) sinh(aτ_p /c), x(τ_p) = (c²/a) cosh(aτ_p /c)</em> where <em>τ_p</em> is the observer&#8217;s proper time. Under the Wick rotation <em>t → −iτ</em> (Theorem 2.1), with <em>τ = x₄/c</em>, the hyperbolic boost in the (<em>x, t</em>)-plane becomes a Euclidean rotation in the (<em>x, x</em>₄)-plane by angle <em>θ = aτ_p /c</em>.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Periodicity in the Euclidean angle <em>θ</em> (required by single-valuedness of the rotation on the Euclidean section) is <em>θ ∈ [0, 2π)</em>. The corresponding period in the Wick-rotated proper time is</p>



<blockquote class="wp-block-quote is-layout-flow wp-block-quote-is-layout-flow">
<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><em>Δτ_p = 2πc/a.</em> <em>(4.6)</em></p>
</blockquote>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">By the KMS condition of quantum statistical mechanics [20], a quantum field state that is periodic in imaginary time with period <em>β</em> is a thermal state with temperature <em>T = 1/(k_B β/ℏ)</em>. Identifying the imaginary-time period Δ<em>τ_p</em> with <em>ℏβ</em> (the standard KMS identification with units restored), we obtain</p>



<blockquote class="wp-block-quote is-layout-flow wp-block-quote-is-layout-flow">
<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><em>ℏβ = 2πc/a · (1/c) = 2π/a</em> in time units, i.e., <em>β = 2π/(ℏa) · ℏ = 2π/(ac) · ℏ.</em></p>
</blockquote>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Equivalently, restoring all factors using the standard derivation [11, §6.7; 17, 18, 19],</p>



<blockquote class="wp-block-quote is-layout-flow wp-block-quote-is-layout-flow">
<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><em>T_U = ℏa / (2π c k_B).</em> <em>(4.7)</em></p>
</blockquote>



<blockquote class="wp-block-quote is-layout-flow wp-block-quote-is-layout-flow">
<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><strong>Theorem 4.3 (Unruh temperature from McGucken).</strong> <em>Given the McGucken Principle and the Wick rotation Theorem 2.1, a uniformly accelerated observer experiences a temperature</em></p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><em>T_U = ℏa / (2π c k_B).</em></p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><em><strong>Proof.</strong></em> <em>The Wick rotation t → −iτ with τ = x₄/c (Theorem 2.1) converts the Lorentz boost in (x, t) to a Euclidean rotation in (x, x₄). Single-valuedness of the rotation requires period 2π in the Euclidean angle, giving Δτ = 2πc/a (eq. 4.6), hence imaginary-time period 2π/a in coordinate time. The KMS identification of imaginary-time period with inverse temperature [20] yields β = 2πℏ/(ac) and T_U = ℏa/(2πck_B). ∎</em></p>
</blockquote>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">The KMS identification (imaginary-time period ↔ inverse temperature) is the one substantive input here from quantum statistical mechanics. It is taken as a standing assumption of the Channel B derivation, alongside the Clausius relation.</p>



<h3 class="wp-block-heading">§4.4 The Clausius relation on local Rindler horizons, and the field equations</h3>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">With the geometric Second Law (Theorem 4.1), the area law (Theorem 4.2), and the Unruh temperature (Theorem 4.3) established as theorems of the McGucken Principle, the Channel B derivation of the field equations proceeds along Jacobson&#8217;s 1995 chain [2].</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Consider an arbitrary spacetime point <em>p</em> and a local Rindler horizon <em>H</em> through <em>p</em>: a null hypersurface generated by a null congruence with affine parameter <em>λ</em> and tangent vector <em>k^μ</em>. The horizon is the boundary of the past of a uniformly accelerated observer in the local neighbourhood of <em>p</em>.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">The heat flux through <em>H</em> is</p>



<blockquote class="wp-block-quote is-layout-flow wp-block-quote-is-layout-flow">
<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><em>δQ = ∫_H T_μν k^μ k^ν dλ dA.</em> <em>(4.9)</em></p>
</blockquote>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">The entropy change is, by the area law (Theorem 4.2),</p>



<blockquote class="wp-block-quote is-layout-flow wp-block-quote-is-layout-flow">
<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><em>δS = (k_B / 4ℓ_p²) δA.</em> <em>(4.10)</em></p>
</blockquote>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">The area change <em>δA</em> is computed from the Raychaudhuri equation [21] applied to the null congruence generating <em>H</em>:</p>



<blockquote class="wp-block-quote is-layout-flow wp-block-quote-is-layout-flow">
<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><em>δA = −</em>∫_H <em>R_μν k^μ k^ν dλ dA</em> (to leading order, neglecting shear and expansion squared). <em>(4.11)</em></p>
</blockquote>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">The Clausius relation <em>δQ = T_U δS</em> with <em>T_U</em> the Unruh temperature (4.7) for the local accelerated observer, applied at the horizon, gives [2]</p>



<blockquote class="wp-block-quote is-layout-flow wp-block-quote-is-layout-flow">
<p class="wp-block-paragraph">∫_H <em>T_μν k^μ k^ν dλ dA = (ℏ a / 2π c k_B) · (k_B / 4ℓ_p²) · (−</em>∫_H <em>R_μν k^μ k^ν dλ dA)</em>.</p>
</blockquote>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Cancelling the common integration measure and using <em>ℓ_p² = ℏG/c³</em>, after multiplying through and rearranging:</p>



<blockquote class="wp-block-quote is-layout-flow wp-block-quote-is-layout-flow">
<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><em>T_μν k^μ k^ν = (c⁴ / 8π G) R_μν k^μ k^ν</em> (for all null <em>k^μ</em>). <em>(4.12)</em></p>
</blockquote>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Since (4.12) holds for every null <em>k^μ</em> at every spacetime point, and <em>T_μν</em> and <em>R_μν</em> are both symmetric tensors, the contraction with null vectors forces</p>



<blockquote class="wp-block-quote is-layout-flow wp-block-quote-is-layout-flow">
<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><em>R_μν − (1/2) R g_μν + Λ g_μν = (8π G / c⁴) T_μν</em> <em>(4.13)</em></p>
</blockquote>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">where the constant Λ enters as an integration constant (the cosmological constant) and the trace term <em>(1/2)Rg_μν</em> is forced by the conservation <em>∇^μ T_μν = 0</em>, which is in turn required by the contracted Bianchi identity <em>∇^μ G_μν = 0</em> [2, 11].</p>



<blockquote class="wp-block-quote is-layout-flow wp-block-quote-is-layout-flow">
<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><strong>Theorem 4.4 (Channel B output).</strong> <em>The Einstein field equations G_μν + Λg_μν = (8πG/c⁴) T_μν follow from:</em> <em>(i) the geometric Second Law dS/dt &gt; 0 (Theorem 4.1, from dx₄/dt = ic);</em> <em>(ii) the area law S = k_B A/(4ℓ_p²) (Theorem 4.2, from dx₄/dt = ic + Planck scale);</em> <em>(iii) the Unruh temperature T_U = ℏa/(2πck_B) (Theorem 4.3, from dx₄/dt = ic + KMS);</em> <em>(iv) the Clausius relation δQ = TdS;</em> <em>(v) the Raychaudhuri equation for null congruences.</em></p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><em>Postulates (i)–(iii) are theorems of dx₄/dt = ic. Postulates (iv) and (v) are standard.</em></p>
</blockquote>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">This is the self-contained Channel B derivation at the <em>horizon level</em>. It does not import the area law, the Unruh temperature, or the Second Law as black-box postulates; each is derived from <em>dx₄/dt = ic</em> as a theorem of the McGucken Principle. However, the Channel B content of <em>dx₄/dt = ic</em> extends below the horizon level into a structurally independent <em>particle-level</em> derivation of the Second Law. We import this from [MGT] in the next subsection as standalone content.</p>



<h3 class="wp-block-heading">§4.5 The Particle-Level Companion: Compton-Coupling Brownian Motion and the Strict Second Law</h3>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">The horizon-level Second Law of §4.1 — <em>dS/dt &gt; 0</em> on the expanding McGucken Sphere — and the area law of §4.2 are <em>macroscopic</em> statements about gravitational degrees of freedom on a horizon. The same Channel B content of <em>dx₄/dt = ic</em> admits a structurally independent derivation of the Second Law at the <em>microscopic</em> particle level, through the Compton coupling between massive matter and <em>x₄</em>-expansion. This derivation is established in [MGT] as a five-theorem chain (Theorems 4–10 in that paper) that we import here as standalone content, with proofs.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">The particle-level derivation is significant for three reasons. <em>First</em>, it produces a <em>strict numerical rate</em> for the Second Law — <em>dS/dt = (3/2)k_B/t</em> for any massive-particle ensemble, <em>dS/dt = 2k_B/t</em> for photons on the McGucken Sphere — rather than only the inequality <em>dS/dt &gt; 0</em>. <em>Second</em>, it dissolves Loschmidt&#8217;s reversibility objection structurally rather than statistically: the dual-channel architecture of <em>dx₄/dt = ic</em> assigns time-symmetric microscopic dynamics to Channel A and time-asymmetric macroscopic monotonicity to Channel B, with the two living at different structural levels of the same principle. <em>Third</em>, the Compton-coupling mechanism is the <em>microscopic particle-level companion</em> to the Huygens-McGucken Sphere path integral of [MQF], and the identification of these two as Wick-rotations of each other is the content of the Universal McGucken Channel B Theorem (§7.9 below).</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">We proceed in five propositions imported from [MGT, Theorems 4–9].</p>



<blockquote class="wp-block-quote is-layout-flow wp-block-quote-is-layout-flow">
<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><strong>Proposition 4.5.1 (Compton coupling between matter and x₄).</strong> <em>Every massive particle of rest mass m has rest-frame phase oscillation at the Compton angular frequency</em></p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><em>ω_C = mc² / ℏ</em></p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><em>as it advances along x₄. The matter-x₄ interaction is the modulation of this Compton oscillation: the particle&#8217;s x₄-phase is ψ ∼ exp(−i mc² τ / ℏ) [1 + ε cos(Ωτ)], where ε is a dimensionless modulation amplitude, Ω is the modulation angular frequency, and τ is the particle&#8217;s proper time.</em></p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><em><strong>Proof.</strong></em> <em>From the McGucken Principle, x₄ advances at rate ic. A particle at spatial rest in the three-slice expends its full four-velocity budget u^μ u_μ = −c² on x₄-advance, giving dx₄/dτ = ic where τ is proper time. The natural oscillation frequency of the particle&#8217;s quantum phase along x₄ is the de Broglie–Compton frequency ω_C = mc²/ℏ, which is the rate at which the particle&#8217;s quantum phase advances per unit of proper time at spatial rest. The modulation form ψ ∼ exp(−iω_C τ)[1 + ε cos(Ωτ)] is the standard parameterization of the matter-x₄ coupling adopted in [MG-Compton]; the proof of its uniqueness given the Compton-frequency identity is in [MGT, §5.1]. ∎</em></p>
</blockquote>



<blockquote class="wp-block-quote is-layout-flow wp-block-quote-is-layout-flow">
<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><strong>Proposition 4.5.2 (Spatial-projection isotropy of x₄-driven displacement).</strong> <em>The spatial projection of x₄-driven displacement is isotropic at each instant. For any infinitesimal time interval dt, the spatial displacement dx induced by the Compton coupling has equal probability of pointing in any direction in the spatial three-slice Σ_t.</em></p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><em><strong>Proof.</strong></em> <em>We derive isotropy from the physical principle dx₄/dt = ic; the static form x₄ = ict plays no role.</em></p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><em>Step 1 (spherical symmetry of x₄-expansion). The dynamical principle dx₄/dt = ic asserts that from every spacetime event p, the fourth dimension advances at rate c in a spherically symmetric manner: the locus of points reached by x₄-expansion in interval δt is the McGucken Sphere of radius cδt centered at p, with the expansion respecting the full rotational symmetry SO(3) acting on the spatial three-slice at p.</em></p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><em>Step 2 (Compton coupling maps SO(3)-symmetric x₄-expansion to spatial displacement). By Proposition 4.5.1, the matter-x₄ interaction couples each particle&#8217;s quantum phase to its x₄-advance at the Compton angular frequency ω_C = mc²/ℏ. Over one Compton period τ_C = 2π/ω_C = 2πℏ/(mc²), the particle&#8217;s x₄-phase completes one full cycle and the particle is redistributed in the spatial three-slice in proportion to the spatial projection of the x₄-expansion direction. Since the x₄-expansion is SO(3)-symmetric (Step 1), the redistribution is SO(3)-symmetric as well: the probability density ρ(dx) on the spatial-displacement vector dx commutes with all spatial rotations O ∈ SO(3), i.e., ρ(O·dx) = ρ(dx) for all O.</em></p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><em>Step 3 (uniqueness of the SO(3)-invariant measure on a sphere). The set of vectors dx with fixed magnitude |dx| = cδt is the 2-sphere S²(cδt) embedded in ℝ³. By Haar&#8217;s 1933 theorem on the uniqueness of left-invariant probability measures on compact groups, applied to the SO(3) action on the homogeneous space S²(cδt) = SO(3)/SO(2), there is exactly one rotation-invariant probability measure on S²(cδt): the normalized uniform measure σ/(4π(cδt)²).</em></p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><em>Step 4 (conclusion). The probability density ρ(dx) is supported on S²(cδt) by the constant magnitude of the McGucken Sphere expansion, and is SO(3)-invariant by Step 2. By the uniqueness theorem of Step 3, ρ(dx) is the normalized uniform measure on S²(cδt). The spatial projection of x₄-driven displacement is therefore instantaneously isotropic. ∎</em></p>
</blockquote>



<blockquote class="wp-block-quote is-layout-flow wp-block-quote-is-layout-flow">
<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><strong>Proposition 4.5.3 (Brownian motion as iterated isotropic Compton displacement).</strong> <em>Iterated isotropic Compton displacement of x₄-coupled matter at successive time intervals produces a Wiener process: the spatial position r(t) of a typical x₄-coupled particle is a Gaussian random walk with variance Var(r(t)) = 6Dt for some diffusion coefficient D &gt; 0. The probability density is</em></p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><em>ρ(r, t) = (4π D t)^(−3/2) exp(−r² / (4Dt)).</em></p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><em><strong>Proof.</strong></em> <em>We construct the Wiener process from iteration of Proposition 4.5.2; the dynamical principle dx₄/dt = ic enters at each step via the McGucken Sphere reachability measure.</em></p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><em>Step 1 (single-step statistics). From Proposition 4.5.2, the spatial displacement dx in any infinitesimal interval dt is distributed uniformly on the sphere S²(cδt) of magnitude cδt. By direct computation on this measure: the mean is ⟨dx⟩ = 0 (cancellation of antipodal contributions by SO(3) symmetry), and the variance per component is ⟨(dx_i)²⟩ = (cδt)²/3 = 2D · δt where D = c²δt/6 is the Compton-coupling diffusion coefficient with δt set by the Compton-coupling rate. <p class="wp-block-paragraph"><em>Step 2 (Markov property from time-homogeneity of dx₄/dt = ic). <p class="wp-block-paragraph"><em>Step 3 (sum of iid displacements). Discretize the time interval [0, t] into N = t/δt steps. <p class="wp-block-paragraph"><em>Step 4 (central limit theorem). The multivariate central limit theorem applies to sums of iid vectors with zero mean and finite covariance. <h2 class="wp-block-heading">§5 The McGucken-Wick Rotation as the Signature-Bridging Coordinate Identification</h2>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Channels A and B do not merely use different mathematical formalisms. <em>In the gravitational and thermodynamic instances of the Schema, they operate in different metric signatures</em>. Channel A is a Lorentzian-signature derivation: the four-velocity budget <em>u^μ u_μ = −c²</em> has the Minkowski signature built into the minus sign; the matter action is integrated over Lorentzian spacetime; Noether&#8217;s second theorem operates on the real-time Lorentzian symmetry group. Channel B in the gravitational and thermodynamic instances is an Euclidean-signature derivation: the Unruh temperature requires single-valuedness on a Euclidean section under rotation by 2π in the <em>(x, x₄)</em>-plane; the KMS condition identifies imaginary-time periodicity with inverse temperature; the Clausius integration runs over a Wick-rotated horizon; the Wiener process measure is <em>real positive</em> on Euclidean-signature paths.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><em>A clarifying remark on the signature structure of Channels A and B across the three instances.</em> The signature picture stated above — Channel A Lorentzian, Channel B Euclidean — is the <em>gravitational and thermodynamic case</em>, where the bridging Wick rotation between the two channels is structurally indispensable to the Channel B derivation itself (the Unruh temperature, KMS periodicity, and area-law entropy in §4, and the Wiener measure of the Compton-coupling Brownian process in §4.5, all require explicit Euclidean signature). In the <em>quantum-mechanical instance</em> of the Schema, however, the signature structure is more subtle and deserves explicit statement, because the Feynman path integral of §7.2 lives in Lorentzian signature with an <em>oscillating phase weight</em> <em>exp(iS/ℏ)</em>, not in Euclidean signature with a real positive measure. The structurally correct universal statement of the signature picture, accommodating all three instances established by the present paper, is therefore as follows:</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><strong>(i)</strong> <em>Channel A is Lorentzian-signature in all currently established instances.</em> The algebraic-symmetry content of <em>dx₄/dt = ic</em> — translation invariance, Stone-theorem unitary representations, Noether currents, Lovelock uniqueness, the four-velocity budget — operates in real-time operator algebra on real Lorentzian spacetimes. The Lorentzian signature is supplied by <em>i² = −1</em> in the Minkowski line element forced by <em>dx₄/dt = ic</em> (Proposition H.1).</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><strong>(ii)</strong> <em>Channel B admits both Lorentzian and Euclidean signature readings, with the McGucken-Wick rotation τ = x₄/c bridging the two.</em> This is the content of the Universal McGucken Channel B Theorem (Theorem 7.9 below). Channel B in <em>Lorentzian</em> signature gives the Feynman path integral <em>K_L = ∫𝒟[γ] exp(iS[γ]/ℏ)</em> with oscillating phase weight on iterated McGucken Sphere paths, producing the Schrödinger wavefunction propagator (the QM instance, §7.2). Channel B in <em>Euclidean</em> signature gives the Wiener-process measure <em>K_E = ∫𝒟[γ] exp(−S_E[γ]/ℏ)</em> with real positive weight on the same iterated McGucken Sphere paths, producing the diffusion equation and the strict Second Law (the statistical-mechanical instance, §4.5), and producing the Unruh-KMS-Clausius derivation of <em>G_μν</em> (the gravitational instance, §4). The two signature readings are <em>Wick rotations of each other under τ = x₄/c</em> (Steps 3 and 4 of the proof of Theorem 7.9): the same geometric object — iterated McGucken Sphere expansion on the McGucken manifold — generates both, and the McGucken-Wick rotation supplies the bridge.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><strong>(iii)</strong> <em>The Signature-Bridging Theorem of §6 is therefore the gravitational-tier instance of a deeper structural fact</em>: Channel A operates uniformly in Lorentzian signature, while Channel B has two signature readings related by the McGucken-Wick rotation, and the agreement of any specific Channel A derivation with the corresponding Channel B derivation — whether that Channel B derivation reads in Lorentzian signature (QM) or in Euclidean signature (gravity, thermodynamics) — is forced by the existence of <em>dx₄/dt = ic</em> as the real geometric source. In the gravitational instance the Channel A and Channel B derivations are in <em>different</em> signatures (Lorentzian Hilbert vs. Euclidean Jacobson); in the QM instance the Channel A and Channel B derivations are in the <em>same</em> signature (Lorentzian Heisenberg vs. Lorentzian Feynman with oscillating phase). In both cases the agreement is forced, because in both cases the underlying Channel B geometric object — iterated McGucken Sphere expansion — is the same and is read in two structural directions.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">The remainder of §5 develops the gravitational-tier case, in which the two channels do operate in different signatures and the McGucken-Wick rotation is the structurally indispensable bridge. The reader should bear the broader signature picture of (i)–(iii) in mind throughout: the <em>gravitational</em> signature asymmetry is the most striking instance of the Schema, but it is not the universal form of the Schema; the universal form is that Channel A is Lorentzian and Channel B is read in whichever signature the relevant physical phenomenon naturally lives in, with the McGucken-Wick rotation guaranteeing that the choice of signature reading does not change the underlying physical content.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><strong>Two derivations of the same equation in two different signatures cannot share a common kernel unless something bridges the signatures.</strong> This is the central observation of the present section, and the bridge is the physical reality of <em>dx₄/dt = ic</em>: the McGucken Principle is the source of both derivations because its Lorentzian-signature reading produces Channel A and its Euclidean-signature reading produces Channel B, with the <em>McGucken-Wick rotation</em> <em>τ = x₄/c</em> as the universal coordinate identification.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><em>A terminological note.</em> We distinguish the <em>Wick rotation</em> (Wick 1954) from the <em>McGucken-Wick rotation</em> (the present framework). The two are formally identical as the substitution <em>t → −iτ</em>, but their interpretations differ structurally and load-bearingly. In Wick&#8217;s 1954 reading, <em>t → −iτ</em> is a formal analytic continuation device justified by the analyticity properties of correlation functions: there is no physical fourth coordinate corresponding to <em>τ</em>, only a mathematical contour deformation that exploits convergence properties of integrals on the complex <em>t</em>-plane. In the McGucken reading, <em>t → −iτ</em> with <em>τ = x₄/c</em> is a <em>coordinate identification</em> on the real four-dimensional McGucken manifold whose fourth axis <em>x₄</em> is physically expanding at velocity <em>c</em> via <em>dx₄/dt = ic</em>: the rotation is not a calculational manoeuvre but the recognition that the Lorentzian time coordinate <em>t</em> and the Euclidean coordinate <em>τ</em> are the same physical <em>x₄</em>-axis read in two notations. The McGucken-Wick rotation is therefore the physical-content reading of the same formal substitution that Wick introduced. Where the present paper treats the rotation as a load-bearing structural bridge between Lorentzian and Euclidean derivations of physical equations, it operates as the McGucken-Wick rotation, not as Wick&#8217;s formal analytic continuation. When citing the historical 1954 device or its standard QFT usage, we use &#8220;Wick rotation&#8221; without modifier; when invoking the McGucken-physical-content reading, we use &#8220;McGucken-Wick rotation.&#8221; Both names refer to the same formal substitution <em>t → −iτ, τ = x₄/c</em>.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">In standard quantum field theory, the Wick rotation <em>t → −iτ</em> is treated as a formal calculational device — an analytic continuation between Lorentzian and Euclidean signatures justified by the analyticity properties of correlation functions [9]. Under this reading, the Wick rotation is a notational manoeuvre with no physical content of its own. It cannot serve as a structural bridge between two physical derivations, because it is not itself physical.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">The McGucken Principle changes this. McGucken (2026) [W] establishes that the rotation is not a formal device but a <em>coordinate identification on the real four-dimensional McGucken manifold</em>: <em>τ = x₄/c</em>, with the Lorentzian time coordinate <em>t</em> and the Euclidean coordinate <em>τ</em> being the same <em>x</em>₄-axis read in two notations. The substitution <em>t → −iτ</em> is the McGucken Principle <em>dx₄/dt = ic</em> written in different units. This is established as the Central Theorem of the Wick-rotation paper [W, Theorem 6], reproduced here as Theorem 2.1, and is what the present paper terms the <em>McGucken-Wick rotation</em>.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">The consequence for the present paper is decisive. The two derivations of the Einstein field equations — Hilbert&#8217;s Lorentzian variational derivation (Channel A) and Jacobson&#8217;s Euclidean thermodynamic derivation (Channel B) — cannot share a mathematical kernel through any formal device. They can share a kernel only through a <em>real geometric object</em> whose Lorentzian reading produces Channel A and whose Euclidean reading produces Channel B. The McGucken Principle, via the McGucken-Wick rotation coordinate identification <em>τ = x₄/c</em>, is that object. The factor of <em>i</em> in <em>dx₄/dt = ic</em> is not notational; it is the algebraic record of the perpendicularity of <em>x</em>₄ to the three spatial dimensions, and this perpendicularity is what permits the same physical <em>x</em>₄-advance to appear simultaneously as a Lorentzian budget constraint (Channel A) and as a Euclidean periodicity (Channel B).</p>



<blockquote class="wp-block-quote is-layout-flow wp-block-quote-is-layout-flow">
<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><strong>Theorem 5.1 (Signature-Bridging Coordinate Identification).</strong> <em>Let SIG_L denote the Lorentzian metric signature (−,+,+,+) and SIG_E the Euclidean signature (+,+,+,+). The McGucken-Wick rotation t → −iτ with τ = x₄/c (Theorem 2.1) is the unique coordinate identification on the real four-dimensional McGucken manifold that:</em></p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><em>(i) is induced by a single physical principle (dx₄/dt = ic);</em></p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><em>(ii) maps Lorentzian and Euclidean signatures onto one another;</em></p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><em>(iii) preserves the physical content of x₄-expansion (the rate c is invariant under the identification);</em></p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><em>(iv) supports two independent derivations of G_μν — Channel A in SIG_L and Channel B in SIG_E — that yield identical field equations.</em></p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><em>Properties (i)–(iv) are jointly satisfied by no other coordinate identification known to physics. The standard Wick rotation of QFT [9] is the formal shadow of (i)–(iv) when the physical reality of x₄ is suppressed.</em></p>
</blockquote>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">The substantive content of Theorem 5.1 is property (iv): <em>the Wick rotation bridges the signatures in which derivations of G_μν exist</em>. This is what makes the dual-channel agreement of Channels A and B not a coincidence but a corollary of dx₄/dt = ic — the agreement is forced by the existence of an underlying real geometric process (x₄-expansion) whose two signature-readings produce the two derivations.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">The Wick-rotation paper [W] establishes that thirty-four independent inputs of quantum field theory, quantum mechanics, and symmetry physics — including the Wick substitution itself, the convergence of the Euclidean path integral, the +iε prescription, the Schrödinger-to-diffusion correspondence, Osterwalder–Schrader reflection positivity, the KMS condition, Gibbons–Hawking horizon regularity, the Hawking temperature, the Matsubara formalism, the canonical commutator [q̂, p̂] = iℏ, the path-integral weight e^{iS/ℏ}, the Minkowski–Euclidean action bridge iS_M = −S_E, the U(1) gauge phase, the Dirac spinor structure, and the Born rule P = |ψ|² — descend from dx₄/dt = ic as theorems. The agreement of Channels A and B on G_μν derived in the present paper is one instance of this broader phenomenon: every physical equation whose derivation involves the imaginary unit i admits a Lorentzian reading and a Euclidean reading, and these two readings agree because they are produced by the same x₄-expansion read in two signatures.</p>
