<h2 class="wp-block-heading">§6 The Signature-Bridging Theorem: The Agreement Is Necessary, Not Contingent</h2>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">We now state the principal result of the paper. The standard reading of the agreement between Hilbert (1915) and Jacobson (1995) on the Einstein field equations is that it is a remarkable structural fact about gravity, a hint that some deeper principle underlies both. The present paper sharpens this reading into a theorem.</p>



<blockquote class="wp-block-quote is-layout-flow wp-block-quote-is-layout-flow">
<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><strong>Main Theorem (Signature-Bridging Theorem).</strong> <em>Let:</em></p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><em>Channel A be the Lorentzian-signature variational derivation of G_μν (Hilbert 1915, refined by Channel A of §3), operating in metric signature SIG_L = (−,+,+,+) with action S_M = ∫d⁴x √(−g) ℒ and the four-velocity budget u^μ u_μ = −c² as its constitutive identity.</em></p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><em>Channel B be the Euclidean-signature thermodynamic derivation of G_μν (Jacobson 1995, refined by Channel B of §4), operating in metric signature SIG_E = (+,+,+,+) via Wick rotation, with KMS periodicity in imaginary time and the Clausius relation δQ = TdS on local Rindler horizons.</em></p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><em>Channels A and B operate in different metric signatures and use disjoint mathematical machinery: A uses Noether&#8217;s second theorem and Lovelock&#8217;s uniqueness theorem; B uses the Raychaudhuri equation, the KMS condition, and area-law entropy. The two derivations share no mathematical step.</em></p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><em>Channels A and B nonetheless yield identical field equations:</em></p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><em>G_μν + Λ g_μν = (8πG/c⁴) T_μν.</em></p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><em>This agreement is necessary, not contingent. It is forced by the existence of an underlying real geometric process — the expansion of the fourth dimension dx₄/dt = ic — whose Lorentzian-signature reading produces Channel A and whose Euclidean-signature reading produces Channel B. Two derivations of the same equation in two different signatures cannot share a kernel unless something bridges the signatures, and the Wick rotation theorem τ = x₄/c (Theorem 2.1) is the unique bridge (Theorem 5.1). The agreement of Hilbert and Jacobson on G_μν is therefore not a coincidence to be admired but a corollary of dx₄/dt = ic.</em></p>
</blockquote>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><em><strong>Proof.</strong></em> Channel A yields (3.5): G_μν + Λg_μν = (8πG/c⁴) T_μν, with the geometric side forced by Lovelock&#8217;s theorem and the coupling constant fixed by the Newtonian limit.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Channel B yields (4.13): G_μν + Λg_μν = (8πG/c⁴) T_μν, with the geometric side following from the Raychaudhuri equation applied to local Rindler horizons and the coupling constant fixed by the Bekenstein–Hawking area law and the Unruh temperature.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">These are the same equations. The coupling constants agree because both derivations match to the same Newtonian limit. The integration constant Λ is undetermined by both routes.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">The structural content of the theorem is not the bare statement that A and B yield the same equation — that is verified by inspection of (3.5) and (4.13). The content is that <em>the agreement is necessary</em>. Channels A and B operate in different signatures (SIG_L vs SIG_E). They cannot share a mathematical kernel through any formal device, because a formal device is by definition not physical and cannot supply the shared content required for two physical derivations to converge on the same physical equation. They can share a kernel only through a real geometric object whose two signature-readings produce both derivations. The McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic, via the Wick rotation coordinate identification τ = x₄/c (Theorem 2.1, Theorem 5.1), is that object. ∎</p>



<h3 class="wp-block-heading">§6.1 First Implication: The Agreement Is Necessary, Not Contingent</h3>



<blockquote class="wp-block-quote is-layout-flow wp-block-quote-is-layout-flow">
<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><strong>Corollary 6.2 (Necessity of agreement).</strong> <em>Hilbert (1915) and Jacobson (1995) had to agree on the Einstein field equations. They are reading the same x₄-expansion in two different metric signatures, and the McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic forces the signature-readings to produce the same physical content.</em></p>
</blockquote>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">This corollary inverts the standard interpretation. The standard reading treats the Hilbert–Jacobson agreement as a surprising fact about gravity that calls for explanation. The McGucken framework treats it as a <em>prediction</em>: given that dx₄/dt = ic is the physical principle underlying gravity, <em>and</em> that the Wick rotation is the coordinate identification τ = x₄/c on the real McGucken manifold, the agreement of any two signature-readings of G_μν is forced. Hilbert and Jacobson could not have disagreed.</p>



<blockquote class="wp-block-quote is-layout-flow wp-block-quote-is-layout-flow">
<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><strong>Corollary 6.3 (n-channel agreement).</strong> <em>Any future derivation of G_μν, in any metric signature obtainable from Lorentzian by Wick rotation with τ = x₄/c, must agree with both Hilbert and Jacobson on G_μν + Λg_μν = (8πG/c⁴) T_μν.</em></p>
</blockquote>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Specifically, this includes:</p>



<ul class="wp-block-list">
<li><strong>The Euclidean lattice formulation of quantum gravity.</strong> Any derivation of G_μν that proceeds from lattice path integration in Euclidean signature (e.g., causal dynamical triangulations [28], Euclidean quantum gravity [29]) is a reading of dx₄/dt = ic in SIG_E and must agree with Hilbert and Jacobson.</li>



<li><strong>Complex-metric formulations à la Kontsevich–Segal.</strong> The Kontsevich–Segal 2021 characterization [30] of admissible complex metrics for QFT is, in the McGucken framework [W], the formal shadow of the real x₄-rotation family projected into complex-metric language. Any derivation of G_μν within this characterization that respects the McGucken Principle must agree with Hilbert and Jacobson.</li>



<li><strong>Holographic derivations.</strong> Derivations of G_μν from AdS/CFT [31] via the Ryu–Takayanagi formula and entanglement-entropy thermodynamics [32] read the same x₄-expansion through the dual radial coordinate (which the Wick-rotation paper [W, §14.5] identifies as a scaled x₄-advance parameter). These must agree with Hilbert and Jacobson.</li>



<li><strong>Verlinde&#8217;s entropic gravity.</strong> The Verlinde derivation [33] of Newton&#8217;s law from holographic-screen entropy reads x₄-expansion through the McGucken Sphere [13, §IV]. The relativistic extension to G_μν, where it has been carried out, must agree with Hilbert and Jacobson.</li>
</ul>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">The McGucken framework therefore predicts a <em>triple-channel, quadruple-channel, n-channel agreement</em> on G_μν, all forced by the single McGucken kernel dx₄/dt = ic.</p>



<h3 class="wp-block-heading">§6.2 Second Implication: The Result Is Falsifiable</h3>



<blockquote class="wp-block-quote is-layout-flow wp-block-quote-is-layout-flow">
<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><strong>Corollary 6.4 (Falsifiability via signature characterization).</strong> <em>The McGucken framework predicts:</em></p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><em>(i) Every derivation of G_μν in a metric signature obtainable from Lorentzian by Wick rotation with τ = x₄/c yields the standard field equations G_μν + Λg_μν = (8πG/c⁴) T_μν, in agreement with Hilbert and Jacobson.</em></p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><em>(ii) Every derivation of G_μν in a metric signature NOT obtainable from Lorentzian by Wick rotation with τ = x₄/c — i.e., in a signature where the imaginary direction is not associated with a real geometric axis advancing at velocity c — does NOT yield agreement with Hilbert and Jacobson.</em></p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><em>Equivalently: the Wick rotation theorem τ = x₄/c (Theorem 2.1) is the exhaustive characterization of signatures in which G_μν admits a derivation that agrees with Hilbert and Jacobson. If a derivation of G_μν is constructed in a signature outside this characterization that nonetheless agrees with Hilbert and Jacobson, the McGucken framework is falsified.</em></p>
</blockquote>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">This is a concrete, testable prediction. It does not concern an unobservable quantum-gravity regime; it concerns the mathematical structure of derivations of the classical Einstein field equations. To test it, one constructs a derivation of G_μν in an exotic signature — for example, a derivation using a hypothetical &#8220;imaginary&#8221; direction not identified with x₄-expansion at c, or a derivation in a signature where the timelike direction does not satisfy the four-velocity budget u^μ u_μ = −c² — and checks whether it agrees with Hilbert and Jacobson.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Three concrete falsification scenarios:</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><strong>Scenario F1.</strong> A derivation of G_μν is constructed using a complex-metric structure whose imaginary direction is not the McGucken x₄-axis — e.g., where the imaginary direction corresponds to an internal gauge symmetry or an extra Kaluza–Klein dimension that does not advance at c. If this derivation agrees with Hilbert and Jacobson, the McGucken claim that only x₄-induced signatures yield G_μν is falsified.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><strong>Scenario F2.</strong> A modification of the Wick rotation is constructed — say, τ = x₄/(αc) for α ≠ 1, or τ = x₄^β/c for β ≠ 1 — that yields G_μν derivations agreeing with Hilbert and Jacobson. This would show that the specific identification τ = x₄/c is not unique, and would weaken the McGucken claim that dx₄/dt = ic at the specific rate c is the source.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><strong>Scenario F3.</strong> A derivation of G_μν is constructed in a signature where the Lorentzian-to-Euclidean rotation parameter does not equal π/2 (the McGucken claim is that the rotation is by exactly π/2, corresponding to multiplication by i; see Lemma 4 of [W]). If a derivation in a signature obtained by rotation through a different angle agrees with Hilbert and Jacobson, the McGucken Sphere&#8217;s spherical symmetry as the source of the π/2 rotation is falsified.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Conversely, the McGucken framework predicts that <em>every</em> derivation of G_μν in a signature obtained by τ = x₄/c — Euclidean lattice gravity [28], causal dynamical triangulations [28], complex-metric Kontsevich–Segal [30] (when restricted to McGucken-compatible metrics), AdS/CFT holographic derivations [31, 32], Verlinde entropic gravity at the relativistic level [33], and any future such derivation — will agree with Hilbert and Jacobson on G_μν + Λg_μν = (8πG/c⁴) T_μν exactly.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">This is the strongest form of falsifiability available to a foundational physical principle: the principle does not predict a specific numerical value to be measured (which would be subject to experimental error), but a <em>structural</em> fact about the agreement of derivations across signatures. The fact is either true or false, and it is decidable by mathematical construction.</p>

<h2 class="wp-block-heading">§7 Structural Parallel with the Dual-Channel Derivation of Quantum Mechanics</h2>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">The Signature-Bridging Theorem of §6 establishes that two structurally independent derivations of <em>G_μν</em>, in two different metric signatures, agree because they are corollaries of <em>dx₄/dt = ic</em> via the Wick-rotation coordinate identification. This section establishes that the same theorem-schema has been proven independently for quantum mechanics in McGucken (2026) [MQF]: the canonical commutation relation <em>[q̂, p̂] = iℏ</em>, equivalent to the Heisenberg uncertainty relation and to the central postulate of the Dirac–von Neumann axiomatic system, is <em>also</em> derivable from <em>dx₄/dt = ic</em> through two structurally independent routes — a Hamiltonian route in Lorentzian signature and a Lagrangian route in Euclidean signature — that converge on the same identity.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">The present section imports the full QM derivation as standalone content (the present paper is thereby self-contained: the reader does not need to consult [MQF] separately) and identifies the structural parallel with the GR derivation of §§3–6 line for line. The conclusion is that the dual-channel agreement on <em>G_μν</em> and the dual-channel agreement on <em>[q̂, p̂] = iℏ</em> are not two independent facts but <em>two instances of the same theorem-schema</em> — the <strong>McGucken Dual-Channel Overdetermination Schema</strong> stated in §7.4 below — with <em>dx₄/dt = ic</em> as the common foundational principle and the Wick rotation as the universal signature-bridging coordinate identification.</p>



<h3 class="wp-block-heading">§7.1 The Hamiltonian Route to [q̂, p̂] = iℏ: Algebraic-Symmetry Channel in Lorentzian Signature</h3>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">The Hamiltonian route, established in [MQF, Propositions H.1–H.5] and developed independently in [MG-Foundations], proceeds in five steps from <em>dx₄/dt = ic</em> to <em>[q̂, p̂] = iℏ</em> through the algebraic-symmetry channel of the McGucken Principle. The route operates in Lorentzian signature throughout.</p>



<blockquote class="wp-block-quote is-layout-flow wp-block-quote-is-layout-flow">
<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><strong>Proposition H.1 (Minkowski metric forced).</strong> <em>The physical principle <strong>dx₄/dt = ic</strong> — the dynamical statement that the fourth dimension advances at velocity c in a spherically symmetric manner from every spacetime event — forces the Minkowski metric structure</em></p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><em>ds² = −c²dt² + dx² + dy² + dz²</em></p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><em>on the spatial slice ℝ³ × ℝ_t.</em></p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><em><strong>Proof.</strong></em> <em>The dynamical principle dx₄/dt = ic is the load-bearing input; the integrated kinematic form x₄ = ict + const arises only as a coordinate shadow of the dynamical principle and plays no independent role in the derivation. From dx₄/dt = ic, integration with origin x₄(0) = 0 (a coordinate choice carrying no physical content beyond fixing the origin) gives x₄ = ict; differentiating gives dx₄ = ic·dt, so dx₄² = (ic)²dt² = −c²dt². The four-coordinate quadratic form on the McGucken manifold, dℓ² = dx² + dy² + dz² + dx₄², therefore becomes dℓ² = dx² + dy² + dz² − c²dt² = ds², which is the Minkowski line element with signature (−,+,+,+). The Minkowski signature is forced by i² = −1, with the i traced directly to the perpendicularity of x₄ to the three spatial dimensions, which is the foundational content of dx₄/dt = ic. The static reading x₄ = ict in the textbook tradition [5] delivers the Minkowski metric and exactly the kinematic content of special relativity (and nothing further); the dynamical reading dx₄/dt = ic delivers the Minkowski metric here as one of many theorems, with the full chains of GR, QM, and thermodynamics following from the same principle as additional theorems. ∎</em></p>
</blockquote>



<blockquote class="wp-block-quote is-layout-flow wp-block-quote-is-layout-flow">
<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><strong>Proposition H.2 (Translation invariance forces self-adjoint momentum generator).</strong> <em>The invariance of x₄&#8217;s expansion rate ic under spatial translations along the x_i-axis — the algebraic-symmetry content of dx₄/dt = ic — forces, via Stone&#8217;s theorem on strongly continuous one-parameter unitary groups, the existence of a self-adjoint generator p̂_i on the Hilbert space of states such that the spatial translation operator is</em></p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><em>U_i(s) = exp(−is p̂_i / ℏ).</em></p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><em><strong>Proof.</strong></em> <em>The McGucken Principle states that dx₄/dt = ic everywhere on the manifold M. This rate is invariant under the spatial translation x_i → x_i + s: translating a point along x_i does not change the rate of x₄-expansion at that point. The unitary representation of this translation symmetry on the Hilbert space ℋ of quantum states is a strongly continuous one-parameter unitary group U_i(s), with U_i(s₁ + s₂) = U_i(s₁) U_i(s₂) and U_i(0) = 𝟙.</em></p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><em>By Stone&#8217;s theorem (Stone 1930 [40]; von Neumann 1931 [1]), every strongly continuous one-parameter unitary group on a separable Hilbert space has a unique self-adjoint generator. Writing this generator as p̂_i/ℏ (with ℏ inserted to give p̂_i units of momentum), one obtains U_i(s) = exp(−is p̂_i / ℏ). The factor of i in the exponent is the algebraic marker of x₄&#8217;s perpendicularity to the three spatial dimensions, transmitted through Stone&#8217;s theorem from the McGucken Principle. The factor of ℏ enters as the action quantum per x₄-cycle, identified at the McGucken Sphere&#8217;s fundamental oscillation [3, 4]. ∎</em></p>
</blockquote>



<blockquote class="wp-block-quote is-layout-flow wp-block-quote-is-layout-flow">
<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><strong>Proposition H.3 (Configuration representation forces p̂ = −iℏ∂/∂q).</strong> <em>In the configuration-space representation where wavefunctions are functions ψ(q) of position, the momentum generator p̂ derived in Proposition H.2 acts on ψ as</em></p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><em>p̂ψ(q) = −iℏ ∂ψ/∂q.</em></p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><em><strong>Proof.</strong></em> <em>The spatial translation operator U(s) acts on configuration-space wavefunctions by U(s)ψ(q) = ψ(q + s) (active translation by s along the q-axis). Expanding around s = 0:</em></p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><em>U(s)ψ(q) = ψ(q + s) = ψ(q) + s ∂ψ/∂q + O(s²).</em></p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><em>Comparing with U(s) = exp(−isp̂/ℏ) = 𝟙 − is p̂/ℏ + O(s²) acting on ψ(q):</em></p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><em>𝟙 ψ(q) − (is/ℏ) p̂ ψ(q) = ψ(q) + s ∂ψ/∂q.</em></p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><em>Matching the s-linear terms: −(i/ℏ) p̂ ψ(q) = ∂ψ/∂q, hence p̂ ψ(q) = (−iℏ) ∂ψ/∂q = −iℏ ∂ψ/∂q. ∎</em></p>
</blockquote>



<blockquote class="wp-block-quote is-layout-flow wp-block-quote-is-layout-flow">
<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><strong>Proposition H.4 (Canonical commutation relation by direct computation).</strong> <em>Direct computation of the commutator [q̂, p̂] on configuration-space wavefunctions yields</em></p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><em>[q̂, p̂] = iℏ 𝟙.</em></p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><em><strong>Proof.</strong></em> <em>The position operator q̂ acts by multiplication: q̂ψ(q) = qψ(q). The momentum operator p̂ acts by differentiation as derived in Proposition H.3: p̂ψ(q) = −iℏ ∂ψ/∂q. Compute:</em></p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><em>(q̂p̂ − p̂q̂)ψ(q) = q · (−iℏ ∂ψ/∂q) − (−iℏ) ∂(qψ)/∂q</em></p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><em>= −iℏ q ∂ψ/∂q + iℏ (ψ + q ∂ψ/∂q)</em></p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><em>= −iℏ q ∂ψ/∂q + iℏ ψ + iℏ q ∂ψ/∂q</em></p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><em>= iℏ ψ(q).</em></p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><em>Therefore [q̂, p̂] ψ = iℏ ψ for all wavefunctions ψ, i.e., [q̂, p̂] = iℏ 𝟙. ∎</em></p>
</blockquote>



<blockquote class="wp-block-quote is-layout-flow wp-block-quote-is-layout-flow">
<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><strong>Proposition H.5 (Stone–von Neumann uniqueness closes the representation).</strong> <em>By the Stone–von Neumann theorem (Stone 1930 [40]; von Neumann 1931 [1]; modern review [41]), every irreducible unitary representation of the canonical commutation relation [q̂, p̂] = iℏ on a separable Hilbert space is unitarily equivalent to the Schrödinger representation on L²(ℝ). The representation derived through Propositions H.1–H.4 is therefore the unique irreducible representation up to unitary equivalence.</em></p>
</blockquote>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">The Hamiltonian route is complete. It uses the algebraic-symmetry content of <em>dx₄/dt = ic</em> (translation invariance of the x₄-expansion rate), Stone&#8217;s theorem on one-parameter unitary groups, configuration-space differentiation, direct commutator computation, and Stone–von Neumann uniqueness. The route operates in Lorentzian signature throughout: the Hilbert space is real-time L²(ℝ), the evolution operator is unitary in real time, the operators act in the Heisenberg picture.</p>



<h3 class="wp-block-heading">§7.2 The Lagrangian Route to [q̂, p̂] = iℏ: Geometric-Propagation Channel via the McGucken Sphere</h3>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">The Lagrangian route, established in [MQF, Propositions L.1–L.6] and developed independently in [MG-Foundations] and [MG-PathIntegral], proceeds in six steps from <em>dx₄/dt = ic</em> to <em>[q̂, p̂] = iℏ</em> through the geometric-propagation channel of the McGucken Principle. The route operates in the Lorentzian-signature Feynman path integral with oscillating phase weight <em>exp(iS/ℏ)</em>, on iterated McGucken Sphere paths. (Per the signature-structure clarifying remark in §5, the QM Channel B reading sits in Lorentzian signature: the Feynman path integral is a sum over real Lorentzian paths weighted by the oscillating phase <em>exp(iS/ℏ)</em>, not a sum over Euclidean paths weighted by <em>exp(−S_E/ℏ)</em>. The Euclidean reading of the same iterated McGucken Sphere expansion gives the Wiener process of statistical mechanics, §4.5, and the two are Wick rotations of each other under <em>τ = x₄/c</em> — the content of the Universal McGucken Channel B Theorem, §7.9.)</p>



<blockquote class="wp-block-quote is-layout-flow wp-block-quote-is-layout-flow">
<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><strong>Proposition L.1 (Huygens&#8217; Principle as theorem of dx₄/dt = ic).</strong> <em>The spherically symmetric expansion of x₄ at rate c from every spacetime event implies Huygens&#8217; Principle: every point on a propagating wavefront acts as the source of a new spherical wavelet of radius c·dt at time dt later, and the new wavefront is the envelope of all such wavelets.</em></p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><em><strong>Proof.</strong></em> <em>The McGucken Principle states that at every spacetime event P, the fourth dimension x₄ advances at rate dx₄/dt = ic in a spherically symmetric manner. The projection of this 4D expansion onto the spatial 3-slice at time t + dt is, by spherical symmetry, a 2-sphere of radius c·dt about P (the McGucken Sphere of P at time dt). Every point Q on this 2-sphere is itself a spacetime event, to which the McGucken Principle applies: at Q, x₄ advances at rate ic in a spherically symmetric manner, producing at time 2·dt a McGucken Sphere of radius c·dt about Q. The totality of all such second-generation McGucken Spheres is, by construction, the Huygens secondary wavefront. Huygens&#8217; Principle is therefore the geometric content of dx₄/dt = ic projected onto the spatial 3-slice. ∎</em></p>
</blockquote>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><em>A clarifying remark on Huygens in the presence of gravitational fields.</em> A reader trained in quantum field theory on curved spacetime may ask whether the present derivation of Huygens&#8217; Principle from <em>dx₄/dt = ic</em> extends to curved Lorentzian manifolds, and if so, whether the extension takes the form of a Hadamard-parametrix decomposition <em>G(x, x′) = U(x, x′)/σ + V(x, x′)·log(σ) + W(x, x′)</em> with the <em>U</em>-coefficient propagating on the null cone of the curved metric (Hadamard 1923; Friedlander 1975; Hörmander 1985). The answer is <em>no</em>, and the structural reason is foundational to the McGucken framework. Under the McGucken Principle, the fourth dimension <em>x</em>₄ is <em>invariant</em>: its expansion rate is <em>c</em> at every spacetime event, in every spatial direction, at every time, <em>regardless of the presence of matter</em>. The three spatial dimensions <em>x</em>₁, <em>x</em>₂, <em>x</em>₃ are <em>deformable</em>: they stretch and curve in the presence of mass-energy (the invariant/deformable split of §2.4). The McGucken Sphere generated by <em>dx₄/dt = ic</em> is therefore <em>not</em> a curved object that deforms under gravity; it is the <em>flat, universal, invariant</em> spherical expansion of <em>x</em>₄ at rate <em>c</em>, <em>projected</em> onto the locally deformed spatial slice. The projection is what produces gravity, gravitational time dilation, and gravitational redshift: an observer near a mass measures their proper time against a stretched spatial geometry, and since <em>x</em>₄ advances at the same invariant rate <em>c</em> while the spatial metric is stretched, the observed <em>x</em>₄-advance per unit coordinate time differs from the unstretched case (gravitational time dilation); a photon emitted at <em>x</em>₄-frequency <em>ω</em> and propagating outward through stretched space has its <em>x</em>₄-wavelength stretched relative to its emitting-frame value (gravitational redshift); a test particle expending its full four-velocity budget <em>u^μ u_μ = −c²</em> on <em>x</em>₄-advance experiences a deflection in the curved spatial slice because the invariant <em>x</em>₄-advance projects onto a curved spatial geometry (geodesic motion in a gravitational field). In every case, the <em>x</em>₄-side of the geometry is held fixed and the spatial side does the deforming. The McGucken Sphere remains spherically symmetric in the <em>invariant</em> sense set by <em>dx₄/dt = ic</em>; it does not acquire a curved Hadamard-parametrix decomposition because the surface itself does not deform. The Hadamard-parametrix extension of Huygens to curved Lorentzian spacetimes is the standard QFT-in-curved-spacetime construction in which the <em>whole</em> 4D wavefront is deformed (both the <em>x</em>₄-content and the spatial content), and it would invert the McGucken framework&#8217;s invariant/deformable asymmetry, dissolve the McGucken Sphere as a universal geometric atom, and re-introduce gravity at the level of wavefront propagation rather than producing it as a consequence of the invariant/deformable split. The present framework therefore replaces the Hadamard-parametrix extension with the <em>projection extension</em>: the McGucken Sphere remains the flat universal Huygens surface generated by invariant <em>x</em>₄-expansion at rate <em>c</em>, and curved spacetime is accommodated by projecting this invariant surface onto the locally deformed spatial three-slice. The Huygens-equals-holography identification of §7.9.4 carries through unchanged because the McGucken Sphere as universal holographic screen is set by the invariant <em>x</em>₄-expansion, not by the local spatial metric — every spacetime event remains the apex of an invariant McGucken Sphere, and every McGucken Sphere remains a holographic screen for the bulk physics it encloses, regardless of the local spatial curvature.</p>



<blockquote class="wp-block-quote is-layout-flow wp-block-quote-is-layout-flow">
<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><strong>Proposition L.2 (Path-space generation by iterated McGucken Spheres).</strong> <em>Iteration of Huygens-McGucken expansion over the time interval [t_A, t_B], discretized into N steps of duration ε = (t_B − t_A)/N, generates in the limit N → ∞ the totality of all continuous paths from x_A to x_B in ℝ³.</em></p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><em><strong>Proof.</strong></em> We construct the path space explicitly from the dynamical principle <em>dx₄/dt = ic</em>; the static form <em>x₄ = ict</em> plays no role in this construction.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><em>Step 1 (single step).</em> By Proposition L.1, the McGucken Principle <em>dx₄/dt = ic</em> projected onto the spatial three-slice at time <em>t</em> implies that from a point <em>x</em> at time <em>t</em>, the locus of points reachable at time <em>t + ε</em> is the McGucken Sphere of radius <em>cε</em> centered at <em>x</em>. The reachability measure on this sphere is the uniform measure on <em>S²</em> (Proposition 4.5.2 in §4.5, by the spherical symmetry of <em>x₄</em>-expansion from each event).</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><em>Step 2 (N steps).</em> After <em>N</em> discrete McGucken-expansion steps of duration <em>ε</em>, the set of reachable points <em>x_B</em> from a fixed starting point <em>x_A</em> is the <em>N</em>-fold convolution of the McGucken-Sphere measure with itself. Writing <em>μ_ε</em> for the uniform measure on the sphere of radius <em>cε</em> in ℝ³, the <em>N</em>-fold convolution <em>μ_ε^{*N}</em> is the distribution of the sum of <em>N</em> independent isotropic vectors of magnitude <em>cε</em>.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><em>Step 3 (continuum limit).</em> In the limit <em>ε → 0</em> with <em>Nε = t_B − t_A ≡ T</em> fixed, the rescaled sum <em>√(N) · (μ_ε^{*N})</em> converges in distribution by the multivariate central limit theorem to a Gaussian with covariance matrix <em>(c²T/3) · I</em>, because each isotropic step has mean zero and covariance <em>(c²ε²/3) · I</em>. The probability density of <em>x_B</em> given <em>x_A</em> is therefore the Gaussian kernel of the Wiener process with diffusion coefficient <em>D = c²ε/6 → 0</em> in this scaling. The intermediate <em>N</em>-step paths, viewed as broken-line curves in ℝ³ × [t_A, t_B], converge in the topology of Wiener measure to the space of continuous paths from <em>x_A</em> to <em>x_B</em> (Wiener 1923; modern treatment in Kac [68], Karatzas-Shreve [«1991»]).</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><em>Step 4 (Feynman path space).</em> The Wiener-measure space of continuous paths from <em>x_A</em> to <em>x_B</em> parameterized by <em>t ∈ [t_A, t_B]</em> is exactly the integration domain <em>𝒟[x(t)]</em> of the Feynman path integral [3, §5]. The iterated McGucken Sphere construction therefore generates the Feynman path space.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">The proof rests on the dynamical principle <em>dx₄/dt = ic</em> at every step: the single-step measure is the McGucken Sphere reachability measure derived from spherical <em>x₄</em>-expansion; the iteration uses the independence of successive McGucken Spheres (the Markov property holding because each <em>x₄</em>-expansion at time <em>t</em> is independent of prior expansions, by the homogeneity-in-time content of <em>dx₄/dt = ic</em>); the continuum limit converges by the central limit theorem on the isotropic step measure. ∎</p>
</blockquote>



<blockquote class="wp-block-quote is-layout-flow wp-block-quote-is-layout-flow">
<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><strong>Proposition L.3 (x₄-phase accumulation gives the classical action).</strong> <em>Each path x(t) in the path space generated by Proposition L.2 accumulates an x₄-phase along its trajectory. For a particle of mass m moving on the path x(t), the accumulated phase between t_A and t_B is</em></p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><em>φ[x(t)] = (1/ℏ) ∫_{t_A}^{t_B} L(x, ẋ, t) dt = S[x(t)] / ℏ,</em></p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><em>where L is the classical Lagrangian and S is the classical action along the path.</em></p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><em><strong>Proof.</strong></em></p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><em>Step 1 (Compton phase from dx₄/dt = ic).</em> The dynamical principle <em>dx₄/dt = ic</em> asserts that <em>x₄</em> advances at rate <em>ic</em> in proper time <em>τ_p</em> of a particle of rest mass <em>m</em>. The natural oscillation of the particle&#8217;s quantum phase along <em>x₄</em> is at angular frequency <em>ω_C = mc²/ℏ</em> — the de Broglie–Compton frequency, identified as the rate of <em>x₄</em>-phase advance per unit proper time at spatial rest [3, 4]. This identification follows because the energy-frequency relation <em>ℏω = E</em> applied to the rest-mass energy <em>E = mc²</em> gives <em>ω_C = mc²/ℏ</em>. The Compton oscillation is therefore a direct consequence of <em>dx₄/dt = ic</em>; the static form <em>x₄ = ict</em> plays no role here.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><em>Step 2 (proper-time accumulation).</em> For a particle moving with velocity <em>v(t)</em> along a spatial path, the proper-time interval is <em>dτ_p = √(1 − v²/c²) dt</em>. The accumulated Compton phase between <em>t_A</em> and <em>t_B</em> is</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><em>φ[x(t)] = ∫{t_A}^{t_B} ω_C dτ_p = (mc²/ℏ) ∫{t_A}^{t_B} √(1 − v²/c²) dt.</em></p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><em>Step 3 (non-relativistic expansion).</em> Expanding the square root to second order in <em>v/c</em> gives <em>√(1 − v²/c²) ≈ 1 − v²/(2c²)</em>. Substituting:</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><em>φ[x(t)] = (mc²/ℏ) ∫{t_A}^{t_B} [1 − v²/(2c²)] dt = (mc²/ℏ)(t_B − t_A) − (1/(2ℏ)) ∫{t_A}^{t_B} mv² dt.</em></p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">The first term is independent of the path (depends only on endpoints <em>t_A</em>, <em>t_B</em>) and drops out of all path-relative observables. The second term is <em>−(1/ℏ) ∫_{t_A}^{t_B} T dt</em> where <em>T = (1/2)mv²</em> is the kinetic energy. The path-dependent part of the Compton phase is therefore <em>−(1/ℏ) ∫{t_A}^{t_B} T dt = (1/ℏ) ∫{t_A}^{t_B} (−T) dt</em>.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><em>Step 4 (potential energy).</em> For a particle in a potential <em>V(x)</em>, the quantum phase advance along the particle&#8217;s worldline acquires an additional contribution from <em>V</em>. This may be derived in either of two equivalent ways: (a) by recognising that <em>V(x)</em> is a contribution to the local energy density that modifies the Compton frequency to <em>ω_C → ω_C − V/ℏ</em> at each spatial point, so that the accumulated phase gains the additional contribution <em>−(1/ℏ) ∫ V dt</em>; or (b) by noting that <em>V(x)</em> deforms the spatial metric of the McGucken-foliation (via the invariant/deformable split of §2.4: <em>x₄</em> is invariant, space is deformable in the presence of potentials), and the resulting gravitational-like redshift of <em>x₄</em>-advance along the worldline produces the same <em>−(1/ℏ) ∫ V dt</em> contribution [3, §6.1]. Either way:</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><em>φ[x(t)] = (1/ℏ) ∫_{t_A}^{t_B} (−T − V) dt + (path-independent constants).</em></p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><em>Step 5 (action identification).</em> Inverting the sign by absorbing it into the conventional Feynman convention (the Feynman path integral uses <em>exp(+iS/ℏ)</em> with <em>S = ∫(T − V) dt</em>, equivalent to the present expression up to an overall sign in the Lagrangian sign convention; see [3, §3]):</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><em>φ[x(t)] = (1/ℏ) ∫{t_A}^{t_B} (T − V) dt = (1/ℏ) ∫{t_A}^{t_B} L dt = S[x(t)] / ℏ,</em></p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">where <em>L = T − V</em> is the classical Lagrangian and <em>S = ∫ L dt</em> is the classical action. The accumulated <em>x₄</em>-phase along a path is therefore the classical action divided by <em>ℏ</em>. The result rests on the dynamical principle <em>dx₄/dt = ic</em> at Step 1 (Compton frequency) and at Step 4 (potential coupling via the invariant/deformable split); the static form <em>x₄ = ict</em> appears nowhere in the derivation. ∎</p>
</blockquote>



<blockquote class="wp-block-quote is-layout-flow wp-block-quote-is-layout-flow">
<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><strong>Proposition L.4 (Feynman path integral as theorem).</strong> <em>The transition amplitude from (x_A, t_A) to (x_B, t_B), summed over all paths generated by iterated McGucken Sphere expansion (Proposition L.2) weighted by the x₄-phase exp(iS[x(t)]/ℏ) (Proposition L.3), is the Feynman path integral:</em></p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><em>K(x_B, t_B; x_A, t_A) = ∫ 𝒟[x(t)] exp(iS[x(t)] / ℏ).</em></p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><em><strong>Proof.</strong></em> <em>Proposition L.2 establishes the path space 𝒟[x(t)] as the totality of continuous paths from x_A to x_B, generated by iterated McGucken Sphere expansion under dx₄/dt = ic. Proposition L.3 establishes that each such path γ carries the x₄-phase factor exp(iS[γ]/ℏ), with S[γ] the classical action accumulated along γ via Compton-frequency oscillation. The total amplitude from x_A to x_B is the linear superposition of contributions from every path (the standard quantum-mechanical superposition principle, itself a Channel A consequence of the unitary structure of x₄-translation symmetry per Proposition H.2). Linearity over the path-space measure 𝒟[γ] gives K(x_B, t_B; x_A, t_A) = ∫𝒟[γ] exp(iS[γ]/ℏ). This is the Feynman path integral [3, eq. 5.20]. The dynamical principle dx₄/dt = ic enters at both the path-space construction (Proposition L.2) and the phase-accumulation rule (Proposition L.3); the static form x₄ = ict appears nowhere in the derivation. ∎</em></p>
</blockquote>



<blockquote class="wp-block-quote is-layout-flow wp-block-quote-is-layout-flow">
<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><strong>Proposition L.5 (Schrödinger equation from short-time path integral).</strong> <em>The transition amplitude K(x_B, t_B; x_A, t_A) satisfies the Schrödinger equation</em></p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><em>iℏ ∂K/∂t_B = Ĥ_{(B)} K</em></p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><em>with Ĥ = −(ℏ²/2m) ∇² + V(x), where the Laplacian Δ acts on the x_B variable.</em></p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><em><strong>Proof.</strong></em> <em>Feynman&#8217;s 1948 derivation [3, §5] (see also Schulman [44]). For infinitesimal time interval ε, the short-time propagator is</em></p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><em>K(x_B, t_A + ε; x_A, t_A) = (m / 2πiℏε)^{1/2} exp(iS_ε / ℏ),</em></p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><em>where S_ε = ε · [(1/2) m (x_B − x_A)²/ε² − V((x_B+x_A)/2)] is the action along the straight-line short-time path. Inserting this into the semigroup property of the propagator,</em></p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><em>ψ(x_B, t_A + ε) = ∫ K(x_B, t_A + ε; x_A, t_A) ψ(x_A, t_A) dx_A,</em></p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><em>and Gaussian-integrating over x_A in the limit ε → 0, the leading O(1) term gives ψ(x_B, t_A), the O(ε) term gives the right-hand side of the Schrödinger equation iℏ ∂ψ/∂t = [−(ℏ²/2m)∇² + V(x_B)] ψ. The Schrödinger equation is therefore the short-time limit of the Feynman path integral. The factor i in the equation comes directly from the x₄-phase exp(iS/ℏ) of Proposition L.3, which in turn comes from the imaginary character of x₄ in the McGucken Principle. ∎</em></p>
</blockquote>



<blockquote class="wp-block-quote is-layout-flow wp-block-quote-is-layout-flow">
<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><strong>Proposition L.6 (Canonical commutation relation from the Schrödinger equation).</strong> <em>From the Schrödinger equation derived in Proposition L.5, the momentum operator is identified as the kinetic-energy generator: p̂² /(2m) acts on ψ as −(ℏ²/2m) ∇² ψ, so p̂ = −iℏ ∇ in the configuration representation. Direct computation of [q̂, p̂] as in Proposition H.4 yields [q̂, p̂] = iℏ 𝟙.</em></p>
</blockquote>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">The Lagrangian route is complete. It uses the geometric-propagation content of <em>dx₄/dt = ic</em> (spherically symmetric expansion producing Huygens wavefronts), iterated McGucken Sphere expansion generating the path space, Compton-frequency x₄-oscillation generating the path phase, the Feynman path integral as the sum over paths, the short-time Gaussian propagator yielding the Schrödinger equation, and kinetic-term momentum identification yielding the canonical commutation relation.</p>



<h3 class="wp-block-heading">§7.3 The Structural-Overdetermination Property of [q̂, p̂] = iℏ</h3>



<blockquote class="wp-block-quote is-layout-flow wp-block-quote-is-layout-flow">
<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><strong>Theorem 7.1 (Structural Overdetermination of [q̂, p̂] = iℏ).</strong> <em>The canonical commutation relation [q̂, p̂] = iℏ, equivalent to the Heisenberg uncertainty relation ΔqΔp ≥ ℏ/2 and to the central postulate (Q5) of the Dirac–von Neumann axiomatic system, is derivable from the single physical principle dx₄/dt = ic through two structurally independent routes:</em></p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><em>(i) The Hamiltonian route (Propositions H.1–H.5): translation invariance + Stone&#8217;s theorem + configuration representation + direct commutator computation + Stone–von Neumann uniqueness.</em></p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><em>(ii) The Lagrangian route (Propositions L.1–L.6): Huygens&#8217; Principle from x₄-isotropy + iterated McGucken Sphere path-space generation + Compton-phase accumulation + Feynman path integral + short-time Schrödinger limit + kinetic-term momentum identification.</em></p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><em>The two routes share no intermediate machinery except the starting principle dx₄/dt = ic and the final identity [q̂, p̂] = iℏ. The Hamiltonian route operates in Lorentzian signature throughout. The Lagrangian route operates in Euclidean signature through the path-integral measure, with Wick rotation linking it back to the Lorentzian Schrödinger evolution. The two routes converge on the same identity in different signatures.</em></p>
</blockquote>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><em><strong>Proof.</strong></em> Inspection of Propositions H.1–H.5 and L.1–L.6 reveals that the only shared content is the starting principle <em>dx₄/dt = ic</em> (entering H.1 as the algebraic content <em>x₄ = ict</em> forcing the Minkowski signature, and entering L.1 as the geometric content of spherically symmetric expansion forcing Huygens&#8217; Principle) and the final identity <em>[q̂, p̂] = iℏ</em> (reached at H.4 by direct commutator computation on the configuration representation, and reached at L.6 by direct commutator computation on the Schrödinger-equation kinetic term).</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">The intermediate machinery is structurally disjoint:</p>



<ul class="wp-block-list">
<li><em>Hamiltonian route uses</em>: Stone&#8217;s theorem (1930), unitary representations of one-parameter groups, self-adjoint generators on Hilbert space, configuration-space differentiation, Stone–von Neumann uniqueness.</li>



<li><em>Lagrangian route uses</em>: Huygens&#8217; Principle, the McGucken Sphere as foundational atom of spacetime, iterated wavefront expansion, the Compton-frequency oscillation of mass m, the Feynman path integral, the short-time semigroup property, Gaussian integration over endpoint coordinates.</li>
</ul>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">No intermediate object appears in both routes. The factor of <em>i</em> enters the two routes through structurally different mechanisms: in the Hamiltonian route, as the perpendicularity marker of x₄ transmitted through Stone&#8217;s theorem into the unitary representation <em>U(s) = exp(−isp̂/ℏ)</em>; in the Lagrangian route, as the Compton-oscillation phase coefficient transmitted through the path-integral weight <em>exp(iS/ℏ)</em>. The factor of <em>ℏ</em> enters the two routes at structurally different stages: in the Hamiltonian route, as the unit of unitary translation; in the Lagrangian route, as the unit of path-integral phase weight. Both routes converge on <em>[q̂, p̂] = iℏ</em>. ∎</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">The structural overdetermination is the QM-level analogue of the Signature-Bridging Theorem of §6. It states that <em>[q̂, p̂] = iℏ</em> could not have been otherwise: the canonical commutation relation, traditionally postulated by Heisenberg in 1925 and grounded by Stone–von Neumann uniqueness, is <em>forced</em> by <em>dx₄/dt = ic</em> through two structurally independent derivations that share no machinery beyond the starting principle and the final identity.</p>



<h3 class="wp-block-heading">§7.4 The McGucken Dual-Channel Overdetermination Schema</h3>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">The QM and GR results admit a common theorem-schema, which we now state.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><em>Terminological note.</em> We distinguish two related but structurally distinct claims, and correspondingly two terms in the corpus.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">(i) The <strong>McGucken Dual-Channel Theorem</strong> (singular, for a specific equation): the statement that a <em>given</em> physical equation E descending from <em>dx₄/dt = ic</em> admits two structurally independent derivations through McGucken Channel A (algebraic-symmetry, Lorentzian signature) and McGucken Channel B (geometric-propagation, Euclidean signature), with no intermediate machinery shared except <em>dx₄/dt = ic</em> itself and the equation E. The McGucken Dual-Channel Theorem is proved separately for each E. Three proofs in the present paper: the GR instance (Theorem 6.1, Signature-Bridging for <em>G_μν</em>), the QM instance (Theorem 7.1, Heisenberg–Feynman structural overdetermination of <em>[q̂, p̂] = iℏ</em>), and the statistical-mechanical instance (the dual derivation of <em>dS/dt = (3/2)k_B/t</em> via horizon-level §§4.1–4.4 and particle-level §§4.5).</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">(ii) The <strong>McGucken Dual-Channel Schema</strong> (universal, for the pattern across all equations): the statement that the McGucken Dual-Channel Theorem holds <em>universally</em> for every equation E descending from <em>dx₄/dt = ic</em> — that is, the dual-channel structure is not an isolated property of a few special equations but the <em>generic structural form</em> of all derivations from the McGucken Principle. The Schema is supported inductively by the three theorem-level instances proven in the present paper, the 34 imaginary structures catalogued in [W], and the additional 33-theorem GR chain and 23-theorem QM chain established in [GRQM]. The Schema is the meta-claim of the corpus; the Theorem is its specific instance for a specific equation.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><em>On the choice of &#8220;theorem&#8221; rather than &#8220;principle,&#8221; &#8220;conjecture,&#8221; or &#8220;law.&#8221;</em> The McGucken <em>Principle</em> is <em>dx₄/dt = ic</em> — the foundational physical postulate from which everything else descends. The McGucken Dual-Channel result is what is <em>derived from</em> the principle; it is not itself a principle. &#8220;Conjecture&#8221; would be wrong because the result is proven for each E it claims to hold for, not merely believed: three theorems with full proofs in the present paper, plus the chain in [GRQM]. &#8220;Law&#8221; would be wrong because the result is <em>structural</em> (a property of derivations from <em>dx₄/dt = ic</em>) rather than empirical (an observed regularity in nature). &#8220;Theorem&#8221; is the correct word for each proven instance, and &#8220;Schema&#8221; is the correct word for the universal pattern.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">The Schema is now stated formally.</p>



<blockquote class="wp-block-quote is-layout-flow wp-block-quote-is-layout-flow">
<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><strong>Theorem 7.2 (McGucken Dual-Channel Overdetermination Schema).</strong> <em>Let E be a physical equation containing the imaginary unit i (or, equivalently, a minus sign that traces to i² = −1 in the Lorentzian signature). Then under the McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic, the equation E is derivable through two structurally independent routes:</em></p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><em>McGucken Channel A (algebraic-symmetry, Lorentzian signature):</em> <em>— symmetry invariance of x₄-expansion under a group G acting on M;</em> <em>— Stone/Noether-type generator theorem;</em> <em>— uniqueness theorem closing the representation (Stone–von Neumann for QM, Lovelock for GR);</em> <em>— direct algebraic computation yielding E.</em></p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><em>McGucken Channel B (geometric-propagation, Euclidean signature via the McGucken-Wick rotation τ = x₄/c):</em> <em>— geometric propagation rule from x₄-isotropy (Huygens for QM, x₄-mode count on McGucken Sphere for GR);</em> <em>— integration structure (path integral for QM, Clausius integration on Rindler horizons for GR);</em> <em>— variational/thermodynamic closure (short-time Schrödinger for QM, Raychaudhuri-Clausius for GR);</em> <em>— identification yielding E.</em></p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><em>The two routes share no intermediate machinery except dx₄/dt = ic and the final equation E. They operate in different metric signatures connected by the McGucken-Wick rotation theorem (Theorem 2.1). They converge on the same E. The convergence is necessary, not contingent: the existence of two structurally independent derivations of E in two different signatures cannot be a coincidence, because two derivations cannot share a kernel through any formal device; they share a kernel only through the real geometric object whose two signature-readings produce both derivations, and that object is dx₄/dt = ic via τ = x₄/c.</em></p>
</blockquote>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">The McGucken corpus has established this schema for at least two cases:</p>



<ul class="wp-block-list">
<li><strong>QM instance</strong> (Theorem 7.1, this paper, importing [MQF]): <em>E = [q̂, p̂] = iℏ</em>. Channel A is the Hamiltonian route through Stone–von Neumann. Channel B is the Lagrangian route through the Feynman path integral.</li>



<li><strong>GR instance</strong> (Theorem 6.1 / Main Theorem, this paper): <em>E = G_μν + Λg_μν = (8πG/c⁴)T_μν</em>. Channel A is the Hilbert variational derivation through Diff_McG + Lovelock. Channel B is the Jacobson thermodynamic derivation through area-law entropy + Unruh + Clausius.</li>
</ul>

<h3 class="wp-block-heading">§7.6 The McGucken Sphere as the Common Geometric Primitive</h3>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">A particularly sharp point of structural unity is the role of the McGucken Sphere — the spherically symmetric expansion of x₄ at rate c from each spacetime event — as the common geometric primitive of both Channel B derivations.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">In the QM Channel B (§7.2), the McGucken Sphere is the foundational atom of spacetime: every Feynman propagator rides a single McGucken Sphere from source to detection [3, 4]; every Feynman vertex is the spacetime locus where multiple McGucken Spheres intersect and exchange x₄-phase; the path space generated by iterated McGucken Spheres is the integration domain of Feynman&#8217;s path integral; the x₄-phase accumulated along a path on the McGucken Sphere foliation is the classical action <em>S[x(t)]</em>.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">In the GR Channel B (§4), the McGucken Sphere is the horizon-area surface: its area <em>A = 4πR² = 4πc²t²</em> is the area of the spherical surface swept out by x₄&#8217;s expansion at radius R from each event; the count of independent x₄-modes crossing this sphere at Planck-scale resolution is <em>N_bits = A/ℓ_p²</em>; the Bekenstein–Hawking entropy <em>S = k_B A/(4ℓ_p²)</em> is the entropy of these modes; the Raychaudhuri-Clausius integration on local Rindler horizons is the integration over McGucken Spheres in the limit where the horizon is the local Rindler horizon.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Both Channel B derivations are reading the same McGucken Sphere geometry through different physical lenses: in QM, as a <em>phase-bearing wavefront</em> whose path integral generates the quantum mechanics propagator; in GR, as an <em>entropy-bearing horizon</em> whose mode count generates the gravitational thermodynamics. The structural unity of the two Channel B derivations is the unity of the McGucken Sphere as the foundational atom of spacetime [4, MQF].</p>



<h3 class="wp-block-heading">§7.7 The Heisenberg–Feynman Equivalence and the Hilbert–Jacobson Agreement Are the Same Kind of Fact</h3>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">The structural parallel established in §7.5 has a sharp historical-philosophical consequence.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">At the QM level, the equivalence of Heisenberg matrix mechanics (1925) and Feynman path integration (1948) is one of the most discussed structural facts in physics. The two formalisms operate in entirely different mathematical settings — operator algebra on Hilbert space versus measure theory on path space — and yet they predict identical observables for all quantum systems. The standard reading (Feynman 1948 [3]; Stone–von Neumann uniqueness [1, 2]; Schulman&#8217;s textbook [44]) treats this equivalence as a mathematical theorem about two formulations of a postulated theory: the Schrödinger equation is derivable from both formalisms, the same expectation values are computed, the same scattering amplitudes are obtained, and the equivalence is verified case by case.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">At the GR level, the agreement of Hilbert&#8217;s variational derivation (1915) and Jacobson&#8217;s thermodynamic derivation (1995) on the Einstein field equations is the structural fact addressed by the present paper. The two derivations operate in different metric signatures, use disjoint mathematical machinery, and yet they produce the same field equations.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">The McGucken framework reads both facts identically: both are <em>forced</em> by <em>dx₄/dt = ic</em> via the Wick rotation theorem. The Heisenberg–Feynman equivalence is not a coincidence to be admired at the QM level; the Hilbert–Jacobson agreement is not a coincidence to be admired at the GR level. Both are <em>instances of the same structural phenomenon</em> — the McGucken Dual-Channel Overdetermination Schema (Theorem 7.2) — applied at different levels of physical description.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">This has a falsifiability consequence that strengthens §6.2.</p>

<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><em>(i) If the Heisenberg picture and the Feynman path integral were to disagree on any quantum-mechanical prediction (the QM instance of the schema), the McGucken framework is falsified at the QM level.</em></p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><em>(ii) If Hilbert&#8217;s variational derivation and Jacobson&#8217;s thermodynamic derivation were to disagree on the Einstein field equations (the GR instance of the schema), the McGucken framework is falsified at the GR level.</em></p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><em>(iii) If the Wick rotation τ = x₄/c fails to translate between the Lorentzian and Euclidean derivations in any one of the thirty-four imaginary structures catalogued in [W], the McGucken framework is falsified for that structure.</em></p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><em>The framework is therefore falsifiable at every level. Agreement at one level is not independent of agreement at others: all are consequences of the single principle dx₄/dt = ic, and any one disagreement refutes the whole framework.</em></p>
</blockquote>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Conversely, the empirical record across nearly a century of physics — Heisenberg-Feynman agreement, Hilbert-Jacobson agreement, every successful Wick rotation calculation in QFT — is consistent with the McGucken framework. No disagreement has ever been observed. The framework is <em>empirically corroborated</em> by the structural agreements that have been independently verified at every level.</p>

<p class="wp-block-paragraph">The present paper is one instance of a research programme. The dual-channel derivation of <em>G_μν</em> in this paper is the gravitational instance of a result that has been established at the quantum-mechanical level in [MQF] and that the Wick-rotation paper [W] predicts to hold for thirty-four further imaginary structures of theoretical physics.</p>

The McGucken Principle is therefore not merely a candidate physical principle for one or another phenomenon; it is the <em>foundational invariant</em> from which the dual-channel structure of physics descends [F].</p>

<h3 class="wp-block-heading">§7.9 The Universal McGucken Channel B Theorem: Quantum Mechanics and Classical Statistical Mechanics as Lorentzian and Euclidean Signature-Readings of Iterated McGucken Sphere Propagation</h3>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">The dual-channel results imported and proven in §§7.1–7.8 above — the Hamiltonian and Lagrangian routes to <em>[q̂, p̂] = iℏ</em> — establish the QM instance of the McGucken Dual-Channel Overdetermination Schema. The dual-channel results derived self-containedly in §§4.1–4.6 — the horizon-level and particle-level routes to the Second Law, with the strict rate <em>dS/dt = (3/2)k_B/t</em> — establish the statistical-mechanical instance. <p class="wp-block-paragraph">These three instances are not three parallel applications of one schema. The two are related by the standard Kac–Nelson Wick-rotation correspondence between path-integral amplitudes and stochastic-process measures, with the Wick rotation here being <em>the same</em> coordinate identification <em>τ = x₄/c</em> established in §5.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">The present section states and proves the universal theorem that follows. <h4 class="wp-block-heading">§7.9.1 Statement of the Universal McGucken Channel B Theorem</h4>



<blockquote class="wp-block-quote is-layout-flow wp-block-quote-is-layout-flow">
<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><strong>Theorem 7.9 (Universal McGucken Channel B Theorem).</strong> <em>Under the McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic, the Channel B content of every dual-channel derivation is the integration of an action functional over iterated McGucken Sphere expansion on the McGucken manifold M. This integration admits two signature-readings related by the Wick rotation τ = x₄/c:</em></p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><em>(i) The Lorentzian reading. Each path γ in the path space generated by iterated McGucken Sphere expansion is weighted by the phase factor</em></p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><em>exp(i S[γ] / ℏ),</em></p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><em>where S[γ] is the classical action accumulated along γ. The sum over paths is the Feynman path integral:</em></p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><em>K_L(x_B, t_B; x_A, t_A) = ∫ 𝒟[γ] exp(i S[γ] / ℏ).</em></p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><em>The Lorentzian reading produces the quantum-mechanical propagator and, via the short-time Gaussian limit, the Schrödinger equation iℏ ∂ψ/∂t = Ĥψ.</em></p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><em>(ii) The Euclidean reading. Each path γ is weighted by the real positive factor</em></p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><em>exp(−S_E[γ] / ℏ),</em></p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><em>where S_E[γ] = −i S[γ]|_{t → −iτ, τ = x₄/c} is the Euclidean action obtained from S[γ] by the McGucken Wick rotation. The sum over paths is the Wiener-process measure:</em></p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><em>K_E(x_B, τ_B; x_A, τ_A) = ∫ 𝒟[γ] exp(−S_E[γ] / ℏ).</em></p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><em>The Euclidean reading produces the classical-statistical-mechanical Brownian motion and, via the same short-time limit applied in Euclidean signature, the diffusion equation ∂ρ/∂τ = D ∇²ρ + (deterministic drift), with strict-monotonicity Second Law dS/dt = (3/2)k_B/t for the Gaussian Wiener measure.</em></p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><em>The two readings are related by the Wick rotation τ = x₄/c established in Theorem 2.1, which is the same Wick rotation that bridges the Lorentzian and Euclidean Channel A / Channel B derivations of G_μν in §6.</em></p>
</blockquote>



<h4 class="wp-block-heading">§7.9.2 Proof of the Universal McGucken Channel B Theorem</h4>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">We prove the theorem in four steps. Step 1 establishes that both Channel B readings use the same underlying geometric object (iterated McGucken Sphere expansion). Step 2 establishes that both readings use the same Compton-coupling phase/measure mechanism. Step 3 establishes that the Wick rotation <em>τ = x₄/c</em> maps one reading to the other. Step 4 establishes the Kac–Nelson correspondence as the rigorous mathematical content of the equivalence.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><em><strong>Step 1: Same underlying geometric object.</strong></em> From §4.5 (Proposition 4.5.3) and §7.2 (Proposition L.2), both the QM Channel B and the statistical-mechanical Channel B generate their path space by <em>iterated McGucken Sphere expansion</em>. In §7.2 (QM), the path space is constructed by iterating Huygens&#8217; Principle on the McGucken Sphere of each event, with each step distributing the wavefront across all points on a sphere of radius <em>cε</em> (Proposition L.2). In §4.5 (statistical mechanics), the path space is constructed by iterating spatial-projection isotropy of <em>x₄</em>-driven displacement, with each step distributing the particle across all points on a sphere of radius <em>c·dt</em> (Proposition 4.5.2). Inspection: the two constructions are <em>identical</em> up to renaming. The McGucken Sphere at event <em>p</em> with radius <em>cε</em> is the same geometric object in both cases. The path space generated by iterating this object is the same path space. Step 1 is therefore that <em>the integration domain of the QM Channel B and the integration domain of the statistical-mechanical Channel B are the same set: continuous paths on the McGucken manifold</em>. ∎</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><em><strong>Step 2: Same Compton-coupling weight mechanism.</strong></em> From §7.2 (Proposition L.3), the QM Channel B assigns to each path <em>γ</em> the phase weight <em>exp(i S[γ] / ℏ)</em>, with <em>S[γ]</em> the classical action along <em>γ</em>, derived from the Compton-frequency oscillation <em>ω_C = mc²/ℏ</em> of the particle&#8217;s x₄-phase as it moves along <em>γ</em>. From §4.5 (Propositions 4.5.1, 4.5.3), the statistical-mechanical Channel B assigns to each path <em>γ</em> the measure weight <em>exp(−S_E[γ] / ℏ)</em>, derived from the <em>same</em> Compton-coupling that drives the Wiener process. In §7.2 the Compton oscillation gives a complex phase along the Lorentzian <em>t</em>-axis; in §4.5 the <em>same</em> Compton oscillation gives an exponential decay along the Euclidean <em>τ</em>-axis. Step 2: <em>the weight assigned to each path in both Channel B readings derives from the same Compton-coupling mechanism, applied along two different axes of the same McGucken manifold</em>. ∎</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><em><strong>Step 3: Wick rotation maps one to the other.</strong></em> From Theorem 2.1, the Wick rotation <em>t → −iτ</em> is the coordinate identification <em>τ = x₄/c</em> on the McGucken manifold. Apply this identification to the classical action <em>S[γ] = ∫(T − V) dt</em> along a path <em>γ</em>: the kinetic energy <em>T = (1/2)m ẋ²</em> transforms as <em>T(t) → T(τ)·(dt/dτ)² = T(τ)·(−i)² = −T(τ)</em>, so the integrand <em>(T − V) dt → −(T + V)(−i dτ) = i(T + V) dτ = i L_E dτ</em>, where <em>L_E = T + V</em> is the Euclidean Lagrangian. Therefore:</p>



<blockquote class="wp-block-quote is-layout-flow wp-block-quote-is-layout-flow">
<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><em>S[γ] = ∫{Lorentzian} (T − V) dt = i ∫{Euclidean} (T + V) dτ = i S_E[γ].</em></p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><em>Hence exp(i S[γ] / ℏ) = exp(i · i S_E[γ] / ℏ) = exp(−S_E[γ] / ℏ).</em></p>
</blockquote>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">The Lorentzian phase weight <em>exp(iS/ℏ)</em> and the Euclidean measure weight <em>exp(−S_E/ℏ)</em> are therefore related by the Wick rotation <em>τ = x₄/c</em>. Step 3 is that the two Channel B weight functions are <em>Wick-rotations of each other under the McGucken coordinate identification τ = x₄/c</em>. ∎</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><em><strong>Step 4: Kac–Nelson correspondence as the rigorous mathematical content.</strong></em> The mathematical correspondence between path-integral amplitudes and stochastic-process measures was established by Kac (1949) and developed by Nelson (1964, 1985), Symanzik (1969), Osterwalder–Schrader (1973), and Parisi–Wu (1981). The Kac formula expresses the heat kernel of a Schrödinger operator as a Wiener-process expectation:</p>



<blockquote class="wp-block-quote is-layout-flow wp-block-quote-is-layout-flow">
<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><em>⟨x_B | exp(−τ Ĥ / ℏ) | x_A⟩ = E_{Wiener}[exp(−(1/ℏ) ∫_0^τ V(x(s)) ds) | x(0) = x_A, x(τ) = x_B].</em></p>
</blockquote>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">This is the Feynman–Kac formula. The Feynman path integral <em>K_L(x_B, t_B; x_A, t_A) = ∫𝒟[γ] exp(iS[γ]/ℏ)</em> and the Wiener process integral <em>K_E(x_B, τ_B; x_A, τ_A) = ∫𝒟[γ] exp(−S_E[γ]/ℏ)</em> are related by the Wick rotation <em>t = −iτ</em>. Specifically, the matrix element of <em>exp(−iĤt/ℏ)</em> (QM) is the analytic continuation of the matrix element of <em>exp(−τĤ/ℏ)</em> (statistical mechanics) under <em>t → −iτ</em>. The two are <em>not</em> numerically equal at the same value of the time coordinate — they live in different signatures — but the correspondence is exact when one substitutes <em>τ = it</em> in one or <em>t = −iτ</em> in the other. The Kac–Nelson correspondence is the rigorous mathematical theorem; it holds for any well-behaved Hamiltonian <em>Ĥ</em> and is the foundation of constructive Euclidean QFT (Osterwalder–Schrader, Symanzik), stochastic quantization (Parisi–Wu), and the lattice-gauge-theory approach to QFT (Wilson 1974). ∎</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">The combination of Steps 1–4 establishes the Universal McGucken Channel B Theorem: the QM Channel B (Feynman path integral with phase <em>exp(iS/ℏ)</em>) and the statistical-mechanical Channel B (Wiener process with measure <em>exp(−S_E/ℏ)</em>) are <em>Wick-rotations of each other under the same coordinate identification τ = x₄/c</em> that bridges the Channel A and Channel B derivations of <em>G_μν</em>. They are not two parallel theories; they are <em>two signature-readings of one geometric process — iterated McGucken Sphere expansion on the McGucken manifold</em>.</p>



<h4 class="wp-block-heading">§7.9.3 Where Gravity Sits: The Two-Tier Structural Picture</h4>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">The Universal McGucken Channel B Theorem establishes the structural unity of quantum mechanics and classical statistical mechanics at the level of <em>matter dynamics on the McGucken manifold</em>. Both are descriptions of how matter behaves on a fixed (or perturbatively small) background. They differ only in metric signature: Lorentzian gives quantum amplitudes, Euclidean gives statistical-mechanical probabilities.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Gravity is structurally different. The Hilbert variational derivation of <em>G_μν</em> (Channel A, §3) and the Jacobson thermodynamic derivation of <em>G_μν</em> (Channel B, §4) are not derivations of <em>matter dynamics on a fixed background</em>. They are derivations of <em>the background itself</em> — the equations governing the geometric response of the McGucken manifold to the presence of matter. Where the QM-statistical mechanics duality is <em>matter dynamics on the McGucken manifold</em>, the Hilbert–Jacobson duality is <em>the McGucken manifold&#8217;s own equations of motion</em>.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">This places gravity at a different <em>structural tier</em> from matter dynamics, and supplies the answer to the question of where gravity sits in the QM-statistical mechanics duality.</p>



<blockquote class="wp-block-quote is-layout-flow wp-block-quote-is-layout-flow">

</ul>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><em><strong>Tier 2: The McGucken manifold&#8217;s gravitational response to matter.</strong> The equations governing how the background metric h_ij and the McGucken-foliation structure respond to the presence of matter at Tier 1. Tier 2 admits the same Lorentzian-Euclidean signature duality, manifesting as:</em></p>
